summary_brief: 2026-04-13，AI Agent 生态进入"SDK 成熟化元年"与"企业生态整合"新阶段。今日 32 个信号（高影响 12 个），信号量级持平昨日，但核心叙事从"基础设施搭建"转向"平台整合与生态成熟"。三大趋势分化：①内存/记忆管理从 OpenClaw 单点扩展为跨项目共性需求（gptme防OOM、LangChain引用计数GC、deer-flow异步修复），安全修复同步跨项目扩散（gptme路径遍历、CVE-2025-47273），构成4月初安全运动→跨仓协同→今日通用工程实践的第三阶段演进；②Vercel AI SDK v6正式发布，mem0多SDK同步进入重大版本，标志AI开发框架从"快速迭代期"进入"成熟稳定期"；③Claude插件市场新增Salesforce Agentforce和Base44，openclaw/openclaw+openclaw/skills合计200 commits，与4月12日高潮持平但功能重心转移至插件化架构重构（按需加载/作用域隔离），是OpenClaw从"功能堆叠"向"工程化平台"演进的拐点。dify以100 commits单仓最高活动量值得关注。

engineering_signals.title: Claude 插件生态快速扩张
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Salesforce Agentforce 和 Base44 同日加入官方插件市场，企业级 Agent 生命周期管理框架的加入标志着 Claude Code 已获主流企业认可为 Agent 开发标准工具链。

engineering_signals.title: Vercel AI SDK v6 主版本发布
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Vercel AI SDK 升级到 v6 主版本，mem0 Python SDK 进入 v2.0.0-beta.0、Node SDK 进入 v3.0.0-beta.0，多个核心 SDK 同时进入重大版本迭代周期，AI 应用开发框架正快速走向成熟。

engineering_signals.title: 跨项目内存管理与资源优化
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: gptme 添加 10MB 文件预览限制防止 OOM，LangChain Core 使用引用计数 GC 优化内存管理，deer-flow 修复异步阻塞调用问题，mem0 修复 CrossEncoder API 误用，多个项目同时关注资源使用效率。

engineering_signals.title: Agent 记忆与上下文管理能力增强
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenClaw 新增 Active Memory 插件实现主动记忆检索，Dreaming 功能增加时区支持和叙事清理重试，gptme 修复 tools 字段验证问题，Agent 的长期记忆和上下文管理能力正在快速成熟。

engineering_signals.title: 安全修复成为跨项目共性工作
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: gptme 修复用户头像路径遍历漏洞、mem0 修复插件配置无效字段导致安装验证失败、fabric 修复 CVE-2025-47273 并配置非 root 用户运行，安全加固在多个项目中同步推进。

engineering_signals.title: 本地模型与自托管能力扩展
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenClaw 新增 LM Studio provider 支持本地/自托管 OpenAI 兼容模型，提供 runtime 模型发现和流式预加载能力，为隐私敏感场景提供更多部署选择。

engineering_signals.title: CI/CD 友好化成为工作流改进重点
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Vercel Blob CLI 新增 --all、--yes、--environment 等 CI 友好参数，Claude Code Action 优化 PATH 预置逻辑，Vercel Python 启用构建缓存加速重复部署，开发者体验和自动化支持持续改善。

engineering_signals.title: AWS Bedrock 集成修复与优化
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: crewAI 修复 AWS Bedrock Converse API 工具调用参数被静默丢弃的 bug，将默认值从 {} 改为 None 以正确触发 fallback 逻辑，提升了多云部署的兼容性。

engineering_signals.title: 平台集成与国际化扩展
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenClaw 增强 Feishu 文档评论会话支持，改善文档 i18n 翻译流程，Vercel 扩展 Go vendored 依赖和域名价格查询能力，多平台集成能力持续扩展。

release_signals.title: Vercel Blob命令重大升级
release_signals.why_it_matters: 51.0.0 版本对 blob 命令进行了重大重构，包含多个 breaking changes（--access 必填、--force 移除、子命令重命名），同时新增 list-stores、empty-store 等交互功能，显著改善了开发者体验

release_signals.title: Vercel AI SDK v6正式发布
release_signals.why_it_matters: Vercel AI SDK 升级到 v6 主版本，Gateway 组件同步更新到 v3.0.96，这是核心 SDK 的重大版本迭代

release_signals.title: LangChain Core引用计数GC优化
release_signals.why_it_matters: 使用引用计数管理继承的 run trees 以支持垃圾回收，解决了内存泄漏问题，提升了长任务运行的稳定性

release_signals.title: LangChain Core流式元数据优化
release_signals.why_it_matters: 减少流式处理的元数据开销，提升大规模流式应用场景下的性能表现

release_signals.title: OpenClaw主动记忆系统
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增 Active Memory 插件，在主回复前自动检索相关偏好和上下文，无需用户手动触发记忆搜索，大幅提升对话连贯性

release_signals.title: OpenClaw新增LM Studio本地模型支持
release_signals.why_it_matters: 集成 LM Studio provider，支持本地/自托管的 OpenAI 兼容模型，提供 runtime 模型发现和流式预加载能力

release_signals.title: OpenClaw插件加载机制重构
release_signals.why_it_matters: 重构插件激活逻辑，按需加载 CLI/provider/channel，按 manifest 声明的作用域隔离，中心化 manifest-owner 策略，减少无关插件的运行时加载

release_signals.title: OpenClaw梦之旅系统增强
release_signals.why_it_matters: Dreaming 功能增加 light-sleep 置信度计算、夜间日记时区支持、叙事清理重试等改进，提升记忆持久化和梦旅体验

release_signals.title: Vercel Blob CLI友好化改进
release_signals.why_it_matters: 51.1.0 新增 CI 友好的 blob 命令参数（--all、--yes、--environment），支持自动化脚本和 CI/CD 流程

release_signals.title: Agent Browser Skills命令
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增 skills 命令用于发现和安装 agent 技能，提供内置评估支持，可在 live browser sessions 中测试技能

release_signals.title: Fabric容器安全加固
release_signals.why_it_matters: 修复 CVE-2025-47273（setuptools 关键漏洞），升级 Go 1.25.9 和 Alpine 3.21，配置非 root 用户运行

release_signals.title: Vercel Go vendored依赖支持
release_signals.why_it_matters: @vercel/go 3.5.0 支持使用 vendored 依赖的 Go 应用，扩展了部署灵活性

release_signals.title: Vercel Python构建缓存启用
release_signals.why_it_matters: @vercel/python 6.30.0 启用 Python 构建缓存，显著加速重复部署

release_signals.title: OpenClaw文档i18n改进
release_signals.why_it_matters: 改进文档翻译流程，处理截断输出、Pi翻译会话恢复，提升多语言文档质量

release_signals.title: OpenClaw Feishu集成增强
release_signals.why_it_matters: 改善 Feishu 文档评论会话，增加更丰富的上下文解析和反应支持

release_signals.title: Vercel域名价格查询CLI
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增 vercel domains price 命令，可查询域名注册、续费和转移价格

releases.summary:
## Changes

### PR [#2091](https://github.com/danielmiessler/Fabric/pull/2091) by [jimscard](https://github.com/jimscard) and [ksylvan](https://github.com/ksylvan): Update Dockerfile for best practices and critical CVE fixes

- Pins Alpine 3.21 and Go 1.25.9 explicitly for reproducible, auditable builds.
- Installs the Go toolchain directly in the builder stage, removing the dependency on an unavailable upstream `golang` tag.
- Upgrades `setuptools` to remediate the critical vulnerability CVE-2025-47273.
- Refreshes the `yt-dlp` installation path to align with current packaging conventions.
- Configures the final image to run as a non-root user, reducing the container's attack surface.

key_changes: 钉住 Alpine 3.21 和 Go 1.25.9 版本，提高构建的可重复性和可审计性
修复 setuptools 的关键安全漏洞 CVE-2025-47273
移除对不可用 upstream golang tag 的依赖，改由 builder stage 直接安装 Go toolchain
更新 yt-dlp 安装路径以符合当前打包规范
配置容器以非 root 用户运行，降低攻击面
ai_summary.summary_cn: 本版本主要更新了 Dockerfile 以遵循容器安全最佳实践。关键改进包括：修复了 setuptools 的 CVE-2025-47273 安全漏洞，钉住了 Alpine 3.21 和 Go 1.25.9 的具体版本以确保构建可重复性，并将容器配置为以非 root 用户运行以降低安全风险。

releases.author: vincentkoc
releases.summary:
OpenClaw `2026.4.12` is a broad quality release focused on plugin loading, memory and dreaming reliability, new local-model options, and a much smoother Feishu setup path.

## Changes

- QA/lab: add Convex-backed pooled Telegram credential leasing plus `openclaw qa credentials` admin commands and broker setup docs. (#65596) Thanks @joshavant.
- Memory/Active Memory: add a new optional Active Memory plugin that gives OpenClaw a dedicated memory sub-agent right before the main reply, so ongoing chats can automatically pull in relevant preferences, context, and past details without making users remember to manually say "remember this" or "search memory" first. Includes configurable message/recent/full context modes, live `/verbose` inspection, advanced prompt/thinking overrides for tuning, and opt-in transcript persistence for debugging. (#63286) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- macOS/Talk: add an experimental local MLX speech provider for Talk Mode, with explicit provider selection, local utterance playback, interruption handling, and system-voice fallback. (#63539) Thanks @ImLukeF.
- CLI/exec policy: add a local `openclaw exec-policy` command with `show`, `preset`, and `set` subcommands for synchronizing requested `tools.exec.*` config with the local exec approvals file, plus follow-up hardening for node-host rejection, rollback safety, and sync conflict detection. (#64050)
- Gateway: add a `commands.list` RPC so remote gateway clients can discover runtime-native, text, skill, and plugin commands with surface-aware naming and serialized argument metadata. (#62656) Thanks @samzong.
- Models/providers: add per-provider `models.providers.*.request.allowPrivateNetwork` for trusted self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, keep the opt-in scoped to model request surfaces, and refresh cached WebSocket managers when request transport overrides change. (#63671) Thanks @qas.
- QA/testing: add a `--runner multipass` lane for `openclaw qa suite` so repo-backed QA scenarios can run inside a disposable Linux VM and write back the usual report, summary, and VM logs. (#63426) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- Docs i18n: chunk raw doc translation, reject truncated tagged outputs, avoid ambiguous body-only wrapper unwrapping, and recover from terminated Pi translation sessions without changing the default `openai/gpt-5.4` path. (#62969, #63808) Thanks @hxy91819.
- Control UI/dreaming: simplify the Scene and Diary surfaces, preserve unknown phase state for partial status payloads, and stabilize waiting-entry recency ordering so Dreaming status and review lists stay clear and deterministic. (#64035) Thanks @davemorin.
- Gateway: split startup and runtime seams so gateway lifecycle sequencing, reload state, and shutdown behavior stay easier to maintain without changing observed behavior. (#63975) Thanks @gumadeiras.
- Matrix/partial streaming: add MSC4357 live markers to draft preview sends and edits so supporting Matrix clients can render a live/typewriter animation and stop it when the final edit lands. (#63513) Thanks @TigerInYourDream.
- QA/Telegram: add a live `openclaw qa telegram` lane for private-group bot-to-bot checks, harden its artifact handling, and preserve native Telegram command reply threading for QA verification. (#64303) Thanks @obviyus.
- Models/Codex: add the bundled Codex provider and plugin-owned app-server harness so `codex/gpt-*` models use Codex-managed auth, native threads, model discovery, and compaction while `openai/gpt-*` stays on the normal OpenAI provider path. (#64298) Thanks @steipete.
- Models/providers: add a bundled LM Studio provider with onboarding, runtime model discovery, stream preload support, and memory-search embeddings for local/self-hosted OpenAI-compatible models. (#53248) Thanks @rugvedS07.
- Plugins/loading: narrow CLI, provider, and channel activation to manifest-declared needs, preserve explicit scope and trust boundaries, and centralize manifest-owner policy so startup, command discovery, and runtime activation avoid loading unrelated plugin runtime. (#65120, #65259, #65298, #65429, #65459) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Memory/active-memory: default QMD recall to search and surface better search-path telemetry so memory-backed recall works more predictably out of the box. (#65068) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- Docs/providers: expand bundled provider docs with richer capability, env-var, and setup guidance across provider pages.
- Docs/memory-wiki: add the recommended QMD + bridge-mode hybrid recipe plus zero-artifact troubleshooting guidance for `memory-wiki` bridge setups. (#63165) Thanks @sercada and @vincentkoc.

## Fixes

- Security/busybox: remove busybox/toybox from interpreter-like safe bins (#65713) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Security/Approval: prevent empty approver list from granting explicit approval authorization (#65714) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Security/Shell: broaden shell-wrapper detection and block env-argv assignment injection (#65717) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Gateway/startup: defer scheduled services until sidecars finish, gate chat history and model listing during sidecar resume, and let Control UI retry startup-gated history loads so Sandbox wake resumes channels first. (#65365) Thanks @lml2468.
- Control UI/chat: load the live gateway slash-command catalog into the composer and command palette so dock commands, plugin commands, and direct skill aliases appear in chat, while keeping trusted local commands authoritative and bounding remote command metadata. (#65620) Thanks @BunsDev.
- CLI/update: respawn tracked plugin refresh from the updated entrypoint after package self-updates so `openclaw update` stops failing on stale hashed `dist/install.runtime-*.js` chunk imports. (#65471)
- Memory/active-memory: keep recall runs on the resolved channel when wrappers like `mx-claw` are enabled, improve lexical fallback ranking, and keep lexical boosts out of hybrid search so recall finds the right memories more consistently. (#65049, #65395) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- Dreaming: consume managed heartbeat events exactly once, stage light-sleep confidence from all recorded short-term signals, wake scheduled jobs immediately, raise dreaming-only promotion enough to cross the durable-memory gate, and stop dreaming from re-ingesting its own narrative transcripts.
- Dreaming/narrative: harden transient narrative cleanup by retrying timed-out deletes, scrubbing stale dreaming session artifacts through the lock-aware session-store path, and isolating transient narrative session keys per workspace. (#65320, #61674)
- Memory/wiki: preserve Unicode letters, digits, and combining marks in wiki slugs and contradiction clustering, and cap Unicode filename segments to safe byte lengths so non-ASCII titles stop collapsing or overflowing path limits. (#64742) Thanks @zhouhe-xydt.
- Memory/short-term recall: allow nested daily notes under `memory/**/YYYY-MM-DD.md` to feed short-term recall, while still excluding generated dream reports under `memory/dreaming/**` so dreaming does not promote its own output. (#64682) Thanks @SARAMALI15792.
- UI/WebChat: hide synthetic transcript-repair tool results from chat history reloads so internal recovery markers do not leak into visible chat after reconnects. (#65247) Thanks @wangwllu.
- WhatsApp/outbound: fall back to the first `mediaUrls` entry when `mediaUrl` is empty so gateway media sends stop silently dropping attachments that already have a resolved media list. (#64394) Thanks @eric-fr4 and @vincentkoc.
- Doctor/Discord: stop `openclaw doctor --fix` from rewriting legacy Discord preview-streaming config into the nested modern shape, so downgrades can still recover without hand-editing `channels.discord.streaming`. (#65035) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Gateway/auth: blank the shipped example gateway credential in `.env.example` and fail startup when a copied placeholder token or password is still configured, so operators cannot accidentally launch with a publicly known secret. (#64586) Thanks @navarrotech and @vincentkoc.
- Memory/active-memory+dreaming: keep active-memory recall runs on the strongest resolved channel, consume managed dreaming heartbeat events exactly once, stop dreaming from re-ingesting its own narrative transcripts, and add explicit repair/dedupe recovery flows in CLI, doctor, and the Dreams UI.
- Agents/queueing: carry orphaned active-turn user text into the next prompt before repairing transcript ordering, so follow-up messages that arrive mid-run are no longer silently dropped. (#65388) Thanks @adminfedres and @vincentkoc.
- Gateway/keepalive: stop marking WebSocket tick broadcasts as droppable so slow or backpressured clients do not self-disconnect with `tick timeout` while long-running work is still alive. (#65256) Thanks @100yenadmin and @vincentkoc.
- Matrix/mentions: keep room mention gating strict while accepting visible `@displayName` Matrix URI labels, so `requireMention` works for non-OpenClaw Matrix clients again. (#64796) Thanks @hclsys.
- Doctor: warn when on-disk agent directories still exist under `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/agent` but the matching `agents.list[]` entries are missing from config. (#65113) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- Telegram: route approval button callback queries onto a separate sequentializer lane so plugin approval clicks can resolve immediately instead of deadlocking behind the blocked agent turn. (#64979) Thanks @nk3750.
- Telegram/direct sessions: keep commentary-only assistant fallback payloads out of visible direct delivery, so Codex planning chatter cannot leak into Telegram DMs when a run has no `final_answer` text.
- Gateway/keepalive: stop marking WebSocket tick broadcasts as droppable so slow or backpressured clients do not self-disconnect with `tick timeout` while long-running work is still alive. (#65436)
- Gateway/plugins: always send a non-empty `idempotencyKey` for plugin subagent runs, so dreaming narrative jobs stop failing gateway schema validation. (#65354) Thanks @CodeForgeNet.
- Gateway/auth: blank the shipped example gateway credential in `.env.example` and fail startup when a copied placeholder token or password is still configured, so operators cannot accidentally launch with a publicly known secret. (#64586) Thanks @navarrotech.
- Plugins/memory-core dreaming: keep bundled `memory-core` loaded alongside an explicit external memory slot owner only when that owner enables dreaming, while preserving `plugins.slots.memory = "none"` disable semantics. (#65411) Thanks @pradeep7127.
- Doctor/Discord: stop `openclaw doctor --fix` from rewriting legacy Discord preview-streaming config into the nested modern shape, so downgrades can still recover without hand-editing `channels.discord.streaming`.
- Doctor: warn when on-disk agent directories still exist under `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/agent` but the matching `agents.list[]` entries are missing from config. (#65113) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- CLI/plugins: honor `memory-wiki` when `plugins.allow` is set for `openclaw wiki`, and pass the active app config into the metadata registrar so plugin-owned wiki commands resolve the live plugin config instead of falling back to defaults. (#64779, #65012)
- QA/packaging: stop packaged QA helpers from crashing when optional scenario execution config is unavailable, so npm distributions can skip the repo-only scenario pack without breaking completion-cache and startup paths. (#65118) Thanks @EdderTalmor.
- Media/audio transcription: surface the real provider failure when every audio transcription attempt fails, so status output and the CLI stop collapsing those errors into generic skips. (#65096) Thanks @l0cka.
- Infra/net: fix multipart FormData fields (including `model`) being silently dropped when a guarded runtime fetch body crosses a FormData implementation boundary, restoring OpenAI audio transcription requests that failed with HTTP 400. (#64349) Thanks @petr-sloup.
- Dreaming/diary: use the host local timezone for diary timestamps when `dreaming.timezone` is unset, and include the timezone abbreviation so `DREAMS.md` and the UI make local or UTC time explicit. (#65034, #65057)
- Dreaming/promotion: raise phase reinforcement enough for repeated dreaming-only revisits to clear the default durable-memory gate after multiple days, instead of stalling just below the score threshold. (#64068) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Dreaming/light-sleep: compute staged candidate confidence from all recorded short-term signals instead of recall-only counts, so dreaming-only entries stop rendering as `confidence: 0.00`. (#64599) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Plugins/memory: restore cached memory capability public artifacts on plugin-registry cache hits so memory-backed artifact surfaces stay visible after warm loads.
- Gateway/cron: preserve requested isolated-agent config across runtime reloads so subagent jobs and heartbeat overrides keep the right workspace and heartbeat settings when the hot-loaded snapshot is stale.
- Cron/isolated sessions: persist the right transcript path for each isolated run, including fresh session rollovers, so cron runs stop appending to stale session files.
- Discord/gateway: clear stale heartbeat timers before reconnecting so zombie gateway callbacks cannot crash the process and drop in-flight replies. (#65009) Thanks @SARAMALI15792.
- Matrix/mentions: keep room mention gating strict while accepting visible `@displayName` Matrix URI labels, so `requireMention` works for non-OpenClaw Matrix clients again. (#64796) Thanks @hclsys.
- Agents/Anthropic replay: preserve immutable signed-thinking replay safety across stored and live reruns, keep non-thinking embedded `tool_result` user blocks intact, and drop conflicting preserved tool IDs before validation so retries stop degrading into omitted tool calls. (#65126) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- Memory/QMD: allow channel sessions in the shipped default QMD scope, while still denying groups.
- Memory/QMD: stop registering the legacy lowercase root memory file as a separate default collection, so QMD now prefers `MEMORY.md` and the `memory/` tree without duplicate collection-add warnings.
- Memory/memory-core: watch the `memory` directory directly and ignore non-markdown churn so nested note changes still sync on macOS + Node 25 environments where recursive `memory/**/*.md` glob watching fails. (#64711) Thanks @jasonxargs-boop and @vincentkoc.
- WhatsApp: centralize per-account connection ownership so reconnects, login recovery, and outbound readiness stay attached to the live socket instead of drifting across monitor and login paths. (#65290) Thanks @mcaxtr and @vincentkoc.
- iMessage: retry transient `watch.subscribe` startup failures before tearing down the monitor, and sanitize startup error logging so brief local transport stalls do not immediately bounce the channel or leak raw imsg RPC payloads into logs. (#65393) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- CLI/audio providers: report env-authenticated providers as configured in `openclaw infer audio providers --json`, while keeping trusted workspace provider env lookup defaults stable during auth setup. (#65491)
- Plugins/install: reinstall bundled runtime packages when the matching platform native optional child is missing, so packaged Windows installs can recover dependencies that were packed on another host OS.
- Memory/QMD: preserve explicit `memory.qmd.command` paths, create missing agent workspaces before QMD probes, and keep the current Node binary on QMD subprocess PATH so service and gateway environments do not fall back to builtin search unnecessarily.

key_changes: 新增 Active Memory 插件，提供专门的记忆子代理，支持多种上下文模式，自动获取聊天偏好和历史细节
macOS Talk Mode 新增实验性本地 MLX 语音提供商，支持本地播放和系统语音回退
新增 openclaw exec-policy 命令，支持 show/preset/set 子命令同步 exec 配置
Gateway 新增 commands.list RPC，远程客户端可发现运行时命令和技能
新增 per-provider allowPrivateNetwork 配置，支持受信任的私有网络端点
ai_summary.summary_cn: OpenClaw v2026.4.12 是一个综合质量提升版本，重点增强了插件加载、记忆和对话可靠性。新增 Active Memory 插件让聊天自动获取相关偏好和历史上下文，无需用户手动触发；macOS Talk Mode 支持本地 MLX 语音处理；同时提供 exec-policy 管理命令、Gateway 命令发现 RPC 及私有网络配置选项，进一步完善了功能和安全性。

releases.author: vercel-cli-release-bot
releases.summary:
### Major Changes

-   feat(cli): blob command improvements and breaking changes ([#15375](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/pull/15375))

    **Breaking Changes:**

    -   `--access` flag is now required for `put`, `copy`, `get`, and `create-store` (no longer defaults to `public`)
    -   `--force` flag removed from `blob put` (use `--allow-overwrite` instead)
    -   `blob store add|remove|get` subcommands removed (use `blob create-store`, `blob delete-store`, `blob get-store`)

    **New Features:**

    -   `blob list-stores` (`ls-stores`): browse blob stores interactively or pipe as a table
    -   `blob empty-store`: delete all blobs in a store with confirmation
    -   `blob get-store` and `blob list-stores` now show a dashboard link
    -   `blob create-store` interactive prompt now shows Private first with doc links
    -   `blob delete-store` now shows connected projects in confirmation and auto-pulls `.env.local` after deletion

### Patch Changes

-   Updated dependencies \[[`6712eb87653784b99327f81ed3dbff44e30038c5`](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/commit/6712eb87653784b99327f81ed3dbff44e30038c5)]:
    -   @vercel/python@6.30.0

key_changes: Breaking: `--access` 标志现在对 `put/copy/get/create-store` 命令必需（不再默认为 `public`）
Breaking: `blob put` 的 `--force` 标志移除，改用 `--allow-overwrite`
Breaking: 子命令重命名：`blob store add/remove/get` → `blob create-store/delete-store/get-store`
新增 `blob list-stores`（别名 `ls-stores`）：支持交互式浏览和表格输出
新增 `blob empty-store`：一键清空 store 中的所有 blobs
增强 `blob delete-store`：显示关联项目，删除后自动拉取 `.env.local`
ai_summary.summary_cn: vercel@51.0.0 是包含 Breaking Changes 的大版本，主要对 CLI 的 blob 命令进行了重大调整：`--access` 标志不再默认为 `public` 需要显式指定，`--force` 替换为 `--allow-overwrite`，子命令命名规范化。同时新增了 `list-stores` 和 `empty-store` 等实用功能，并增强了交互式体验。依赖方面更新了 @vercel/python 到 6.30.0。

releases.author: steipete
releases.summary:
### Changes

- Dreaming/memory-wiki: add ChatGPT import ingestion plus new `Imported Insights` and `Memory Palace` diary subtabs so Dreaming can inspect imported source chats, compiled wiki pages, and full source pages directly from the UI. (#64505)
- Control UI/webchat: render assistant media/reply/voice directives as structured chat bubbles, add the `[embed ...]` rich output tag, and gate external embed URLs behind config. (#64104)
- Tools/video_generate: add URL-only generated asset delivery, typed `providerOptions`, reference audio inputs, per-asset role hints, `adaptive` aspect-ratio support, and a higher image-input cap so video providers can expose richer generation modes without forcing large files into memory. (#61987, #61988) Thanks @xieyongliang.
- Feishu: improve document comment sessions with richer context parsing, comment reactions, and typing feedback so document-thread conversations behave more like chat conversations. (#63785)
- Microsoft Teams: add reaction support, reaction listing, Graph pagination, and delegated OAuth setup for sending reactions while preserving application-auth read paths. (#51646)
- Plugins: allow plugin manifests to declare activation and setup descriptors so plugin setup flows can describe required auth, pairing, and configuration steps without hardcoded core special cases. (#64780)
- Ollama: cache `/api/show` context-window and capability metadata during model discovery so repeated picker refreshes stop refetching unchanged models, while still retrying after empty responses and invalidating on digest changes. (#64753) Thanks @ImLukeF.
- Models/providers: surface how configured OpenAI-compatible endpoints are classified in embedded-agent debug logs, so local and proxy routing issues are easier to diagnose. (#64754) Thanks @ImLukeF.
- QA/parity: add the GPT-5.4 vs Opus 4.6 agentic parity report gate with shared scenario coverage checks, stricter evidence heuristics, and skipped-scenario accounting for maintainer review. (#64441) Thanks @100yenadmin.

### Fixes

- OpenAI/Codex OAuth: stop rewriting the upstream authorize URL scopes so new Codex sign-ins do not fail with `invalid_scope` before returning an authorization code. (#64713) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Audio transcription: disable pinned DNS only for OpenAI-compatible multipart requests, while still validating hostnames, so OpenAI, Groq, and Mistral transcription works again without weakening other request paths. (#64766) Thanks @GodsBoy.
- macOS/Talk Mode: after granting microphone permission on first enable, continue starting Talk Mode instead of requiring a second toggle. (#62459) Thanks @ggarber.
- Control UI/webchat: persist agent-run TTS audio replies into webchat history and preserve interleaved tool card pairing so generated audio and mixed tool output stay attached to the right messages. (#63514) Thanks @bittoby.
- WhatsApp: honor the configured default account when the active listener helper is used without an explicit account id, so named default accounts do not get registered under `default`. (#53918) Thanks @yhyatt.
- ACP/agents: suppress commentary-phase child assistant relay text in ACP parent stream updates, so spawned child runs stop leaking internal progress chatter into the parent session. Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Agents/timeouts: honor explicit run timeouts in the LLM idle watchdog and align default timeout config so slow models can keep working until the configured limit instead of using the wrong idle window.
- Config: include `asyncCompletion` in the generated zod schema so documented async completion config no longer fails with an unrecognized-key error. (#63618)
- Google/Veo: stop sending the unsupported `numberOfVideos` request field so Gemini Developer API Veo runs do not fail before OpenClaw can complete the intended Google video generation path. (#64723) Thanks @velvet-shark.
- QA/packaging: stop packaged CLI startup and completion cache generation from reading repo-only QA scenario markdown, ship the bundled QA scenario pack in npm releases, and keep `openclaw completion --write-state` working even if QA setup is broken. (#64648) Thanks @obviyus.
- Codex/QA: keep Codex app-server coordination chatter out of visible replies, add a live QA leak scenario, and classify leaked harness meta text as a QA failure instead of a successful reply. Thanks @vincentkoc.
- WhatsApp: route `message react` through the gateway-owned action path so reactions use the live WhatsApp listener in both DM and group chats, matching `message send` and `message poll`. Thanks @mcaxtr.
- Auto-reply/WhatsApp: preserve inbound image attachment notes after media understanding so image edits keep the real saved media path instead of hallucinating a missing local path. (#64918) Thanks @ngutman.
- Telegram/sessions: keep topic-scoped session initialization on the canonical topic transcript path when inbound turns omit `MessageThreadId`, so one topic session no longer alternates between bare and topic-qualified transcript files. (#64869) Thanks @jalehman.
- Agents/failover: scope assistant-side fallback classification and surfaced provider errors to the current attempt instead of stale session history, so cross-provider fallback runs stop inheriting the previous provider's failure. (#62907) Thanks @stainlu.
- MiniMax/OAuth: write `api: "anthropic-messages"` and `authHeader: true` into the `minimax-portal` config patch during `openclaw configure`, so re-authenticated portal setups keep Bearer auth routing working. (#64964) Thanks @ryanlee666.

### New Features

- **`skills` command** - Added `agent-browser skills` command for discovering and installing agent skills, with built-in evaluation support for testing skills against live browser sessions (#1225, #1227)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **custom viewport dimensions** not being used in streaming frame metadata and image resolution (#1033)
- Fixed **`--ignore-https-errors`** not being re-applied to recording contexts, causing TLS errors during screen recordings (#1178)
- Fixed **duplicate option numbering** in the auth skill documentation (#1161)

### Documentation

- The docs site header now **dynamically fetches** the GitHub star count (#1202)

issue_insights.summary_brief: 本次扫描发现 5 大跨仓库共性问题，其中 Git 环境隔离失败（140 个仓库）、JSON 输出广告污染（40 个仓库）、多平台启动崩溃（33 个仓库）均为 P0 级别。问题主要集中在 workflow_runtime（会话状态、Git 隔离）、auth_permission（OAuth/订阅/Bedrock 认证）、ui_interaction（格式渲染、主题崩溃）和 quota_rate_limit（成本追踪、速率限制）等类别。
global_highlights: Git 环境隔离失败是影响范围最广的跨仓库问题，涉及 140 个仓库，导致 Windows 下 worktree 任务初始化直接中止（P0，置信度 100%）
LLM 成本追踪在会话恢复后静默失效，OpenDevin 实测追踪率从 77.2% 暴跌至 1.8%，多 Agent 框架均受影响
Anthropic 多 SDK 出现认证回归：Claude Code Action v1.0.90 破坏 Bedrock SigV4 签名（403 错误），Claude Agent SDK Python 在 429 时直接崩溃而非重试
Claude Code TypeScript SDK 的 SSE ping 事件被静默丢弃，导致下游客户端产生假阳性看门狗超时，长思考场景（60-120s 静默期）直接触发硬错误

source_issues.title: fix(agent): Git environment isolation to prevent worktree operation failures
source_issues.evidence: Git operations in _unstage_gitignored_files() fail with index file error during worktree creation. Task enters human_review status without completing. source_issues.title: LLM cost tracking stops after session resume — Telemetry.metrics not updated in restore_metrics
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: LLM.restore_metrics() updates self._metrics but NOT self._telemetry.metrics. After resume, telemetry writes to stale empty Metrics while persisted costs[] never gets updated. Real data: go-zero repo resumed had 45 tracked calls vs ~2494 actual calls (1.8% tracking rate, $0.48 reported vs likely $26+ actual). ripgrep fresh sessions tracked 77.2%. One-line fix identified but unfixed.

source_issues.title: Custom skills in container parameter break prompt caching - consistent skills list produces non-deterministic cache prefix
source_issues.evidence: Concrete token-level evidence: with skills, Turn 2 reads cache_read=0 instead of expected ~37097 tokens. Without skills, same pattern gives cache_read=35301 and cache_write=155. Skills list is a compile-time constant — server-side resolution produces non-deterministic output. signals.topic: Dataset JSON uploads silently discard explicit empty outputs and metadata lists causing data corruption
signals.summary: When users upload JSON datasets with explicit empty `outputs=[]` or `metadata=[]` lists, the server-side validation treats them as falsy and skips the length check against `inputs`. Each example is then silently stored with an empty dict `{}` instead of raising a length mismatch validation error. The same truthiness-based omission exists in the Python client-side upload helpers, causing callers who accidentally materialize an empty iterable to silently lose those fields before the request is even sent.
aliases: Dataset JSON ingestion validates empty lists as falsy causing data loss
Empty outputs/metadata silently replaced with empty dict on dataset upload
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed data corruption bug. When users explicitly provide empty outputs/metadata lists, the server silently stores empty dicts for every example instead of raising a validation error for length mismatch. This is a silent failure that corrupts user data without any warning, meeting the 'workflow_runtime' + '反复失败' criteria. The bug has detailed reproduction steps, a root cause analysis, and was closed with community engagement, indicating real user impact beyond theoretical concern.

source_issues.title: Dataset JSON uploads silently discard explicit empty `outputs` and `metadata` lists
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with complete root cause analysis: server-side `if v` truthiness check in datasets.py causes explicit empty lists to skip validation; client-side helpers also omit empty lists before sending. Reproducible with inputs=[{...}, {...}], outputs=[], metadata=[] resulting in silent data corruption where all examples get output={} instead of a validation error. Closed with 5 comments indicating active engagement.

signals.topic: Integration notifications (Slack V1, Jira Cloud/DC) use wrong markup format — bold/links render as raw text

source_issues.title: LLM cost tracking stops after session resume — Telemetry.metrics not updated in restore_metrics

signals.topic: Agent fails to read and execute SKILL.md files, bypassing skill workflow and falling back to generic tools

signals.review_reason: The agent fails to follow its own skill-execution protocol: it acknowledges the skill in the system prompt, promises to read SKILL.md, but instead directly calls generic shell commands. This is a clear workflow deviation that causes the skill to fail. Though count=1, the severity is high (core feature — skill execution — is non-functional for any registered skill), and it is actively discussed with 4 comments indicating community interest.

source_issues.title: AgentScope SKILL 执行问题

signals.topic: Memory component API signature mismatch causes TypeError and runtime crash in example scripts
signals.summary: The short_term_memory_example.py crashes with TypeError: ReMeShortTermMemory.get_memory() got an unexpected keyword argument 'exclude_mark'. This is a breaking API change in the memory module that causes any example using ReMeShortTermMemory to fail at runtime.
signals.review_reason: Official example script crashes with TypeError, completely blocking user from running the short-term memory feature. This is a clear main-flow failure where the provided example code cannot execute at all. Count=1 but the impact is high — it breaks a documented example path and indicates an uncaught API mismatch in the memory subsystem.

signals.topic: AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory with Memory Compression enabled throws foreign key constraint violation, preventing message compression
signals.summary: When using AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory with compression enabled (CompressionConfig.enable=True), the bulk_insert_mappings for message_mark is executed before flushing pending messages to the message table, causing a foreign key violation (IntegrityError). This blocks the memory compression workflow entirely for PostgreSQL async users.
signals.review_reason: Memory compression is a key feature for handling long conversations, but with AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory it throws a foreign key violation and completely fails. This is a feature-specific but critical block for users relying on async SQLAlchemy memory with compression — the feature cannot be used at all.

source_issues.title: [Bug]:Short-term memory使用AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory式，如果开启Memory Compression时，运行报错
source_issues.evidence: With AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory and CompressionConfig(enable=True), bulk_insert_mappings inserts message_mark rows referencing msg_ids not yet in the message table, causing sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: ForeignKeyViolationError. The compression feature is entirely non-functional for async PostgreSQL users.

signals.topic: Session data loss during concurrent writes — upsert_session overwrites entire JSONB runs array
signals.summary: Concurrent arun() calls sharing the same session_id silently lose runs because upsert_session reads the session, appends the new run in memory, then writes back the entire array. When two writes race, the second writer overwrites the first with no error or warning.
aliases: JSONB runs array overwrite data loss
signals.review_reason: Critical data loss bug in the storage layer causing complete failure of concurrent session handling. User runs are silently lost with no error signal, making this a main workflow blocker for any multi-threaded or concurrent agent usage.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Session runs lost under concurrent writes — upsert_session overwrites entire JSONB runs array
source_issues.evidence: Concurrent arun() calls sharing same session_id silently lose runs. upsert_session reads session, appends new run in memory, then writes back entire array. When two runs save concurrently, second writer overwrites first — data loss with no error or warning.

signals.topic: OpenRouterResponses schema incompatibility breaks xAI/Grok structured output (HTTP 400)
signals.summary: OpenRouterResponses inherits from OpenAIResponses which unconditionally injects additionalProperties: false into schemas. xAI/Grok rejects these with HTTP 400, making structured output completely unavailable for these providers.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (structured output) is completely unavailable for xAI/Grok users routing through OpenRouter. Every request to these providers fails with HTTP 400, making the integration unusable for a mainstream model provider.

source_issues.title: [Bug] OpenRouterResponses injects additionalProperties: false into schemas for non-OpenAI providers (xAI/Grok rejects with 400)
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 error returned from xAI provider — schema validation failed because additionalProperties: false is injected into output_schema. Users cannot use structured output with xAI/Grok via OpenRouter.

signals.topic: RemoteDb routes crash with AttributeError when sort_order parameter is omitted

signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure — RemoteDb API endpoints completely crash for any user who does not explicitly provide sort_order. The routes are broken by default, not just under edge conditions.

source_issues.title: [Bug] RemoteDb routes define sort_order with a raw string default instead of SortOrder.DESC
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'value'. Four routers define sort_order as Optional[SortOrder] but give raw string default 'desc' instead of SortOrder.DESC, causing crash on FastAPI when sort_order is omitted.

signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure — TeamSession storage path is completely broken on SingleStore for any session that has a summary. Users cannot retrieve their team session history.

source_issues.title: SingleStore team-session reads crash when a stored summary is present

aliases: workflow step image passing filepath ignored
signals.review_reason: Key feature (image passthrough across workflow steps) is unavailable when images are provided via filepath rather than URL or content. Users relying on filepath-based image inputs in workflows see their images silently dropped.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Workflow pass images to next step failed with filepath=xxx
source_issues.evidence: ImageArtifact with filepath is skipped with warning 'Skipping ImageArtifact with no URL or content'. _convert_image_artifacts_to_images() does not process img_artifact.filepath, only url and content fields.

signals.topic: GPT-5 models with @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider cause BadRequestError due to unconditional reasoningSummary injection
signals.summary: When using @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider (e.g. LiteLLM proxy) with GPT-5.x models, opencode unconditionally injects `reasoningSummary: "auto"` into provider options. LiteLLM rejects this unknown parameter with `litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Unknown parameter: 'reasoningSummary'`. The bug exists in `packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts` `options()` function which lacks the provider-scoping check that `variants()` already correctly implements.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm complete flow block: GPT-5 users with openai-compatible providers (e.g. LiteLLM) cannot make any API call — requests immediately fail with BadRequestError. No config-level workaround exists due to mergeDeep behavior. Count=2 with identical root cause establishes this as a recurring user-blocking issue, not an isolated edge case.

source_issues.title: reasoningSummary injected for gpt-5 models on @ai-sdk/openai-compatible providers causes litellm errors
source_issues.evidence: litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Unknown parameter: 'reasoningSummary'. User provides config with @ai-sdk/openai-compatible via LiteLLM proxy. Both null and undefined workarounds fail due to mergeDeep behavior.

source_issues.title: reasoningSummary injected for gpt-5 models on @ai-sdk/openai-compatible providers causes litellm errors
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report of same root cause: unconditional reasoningSummary injection for GPT-5 on openai-compatible provider. Confirms the issue is reproducible and not an isolated case.

signals.topic: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() uses omitzero dropping required error_code field, causing 400 on agentic loop retry
signals.summary: When the API returns a tool search error, the ToParam() re-serialization path drops the required error_code field because the ErrorCode field uses json:"error_code,omitzero" and the zero value is empty string. This causes the next agentic-loop API call to fail with 400 'Field required', breaking multi-turn agentic workflows.
aliases: tool search result block re-serialization drops required field
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked: multi-turn agentic conversations fail with 400 after the first tool search error, preventing any retry. This is not a one-off edge case — it directly breaks the agentic loop retry path, which is the primary use case for tool search features. Confirmed in v1.35.0 and v1.34.0. Related issue #242 shows this is a recurring pattern across similar block types.

source_issues.title: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops required error_code field via omitzero
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 'error_code: Field required' on next agentic-loop iteration when ToolSearchToolResultBlock with error is re-serialized via ToParam(). Breaks multi-turn agentic workflows. Related to issue #242 (same class of bug with WebSearchToolResultBlock).

signals.topic: BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage helper omits required Type field, causing 400 on POST /v1/sessions/{id}/events
signals.summary: The BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage() helper function constructs BetaManagedAgentsUserMessageEventParams without setting the required Type field, resulting in 400 Bad Request with 'events[0].type: Field required' whenever users call the sessions events API using this helper.
aliases: sessions events API helper missing required field
signals.review_reason: The helper function is broken by design — it always omits a required field, so every user who uses it will encounter a 400. This blocks the core workflow of sending user message events in managed agent sessions, which is the primary purpose of this helper API.

source_issues.title: BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage helper omits required Type field
source_issues.evidence: Calling POST /v1/sessions/{id}/events using the BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage helper always fails with 400 Bad Request: 'events[0].type: Field required'. Reproduction is deterministic — any user who follows the SDK's own documentation/pattern to send user message events through the helper will hit this error.

signals.topic: Structured Output generates all Java fields as required in JSON Schema, ignoring @Nullable/Optional markers, causing LLM hallucination
signals.summary: When using StructuredMessageCreateParams with outputConfig in Java, the schema generator treats all Java class/record fields as mandatory (required: true) in the generated JSON Schema, regardless of @Nullable annotations or Optional<T> types. This forces the LLM to hallucinate placeholder values for genuinely optional fields.
aliases: Java nullability ignored in schema generation
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user pain point with direct evidence: the schema generator's behavior causes the LLM to hallucinate placeholder values for optional fields, directly degrading the quality of structured outputs. The user provided a reproducible code example showing that all four nullability marking strategies in Java (@Nullable annotations, @JsonProperty, Optional<T>) fail to produce the intended schema behavior. While count=1 limits it to P2, the impact is real and UX-blocking for Java SDK users relying on structured output with optional fields.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports that @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and Optional<T> all fail to remove fields from the required array. The LLM is forced to hallucinate 'null' strings, empty strings, or dashes to satisfy schema constraints, degrading output quality.

signals.topic: Managed Agents streaming (client.beta.sessions.events.stream) silently drops all events
signals.summary: client.beta.sessions.events.stream() yields zero events because the Stream class only handles Messages API event types and silently drops all Managed Agents event types (session.status_*, agent.message, agent.tool_use, etc.).
aliases: Sessions events stream returns empty iterator
signals.review_reason: The streaming path for a key Managed Agents feature returns zero events due to a hardcoded event type whitelist in Stream.__stream__. This is a complete functional break (not partial degradation) with a complete minimal repro demonstrating 0/3 events received. The user's claim of full ecosystem impact is supported by the code evidence.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Managed Agents: client.beta.sessions.events.stream() silently drops all events

signals.topic: Custom skills in container parameter break message-level prompt caching — increased token cost per request

Prompt caching fails with custom skills in container

User provides a clear root hypothesis (server-side non-deterministic skill resolution). Impact is confirmed and measurable.

source_issues.title: Custom skills in container parameter break prompt caching - consistent skills list produces non-deterministic cache prefix
source_issues.evidence: Concrete token-level evidence: with skills, Turn 2 reads cache_read=0 instead of expected ~37097 tokens. Without skills, same pattern gives cache_read=35301 and cache_write=155. Skills list is a compile-time constant — server-side resolution produces non-deterministic output. 'Any API user with custom skills cannot benefit from message-level prompt caching'.

signals.topic: pdfplumber completely broken in code_execution sandbox — missing mypyc C extension module
signals.summary: pdfplumber is advertised as pre-installed in the code_execution sandbox but fails immediately on import due to a missing mypyc-compiled C extension module (charset_normalizer). Users relying on the agent to choose pdfplumber for PDF extraction hit this error.
aliases: charset_normalizer mypyc module missing in sandbox
signals.review_reason: A documented pre-installed package fails on first use with a complete traceback. This is a key PDF extraction capability (documented as available) that is entirely non-functional. The mypyc extension failure is a clear sandbox image packaging bug, not a user-side issue.

source_issues.title: pdfplumber broken in code_execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc module missing
source_issues.evidence: Full traceback provided: import pdfplumber immediately raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '81d243bd2c585b0f4821__mypyc'. 'pdfplumber is documented as a pre-installed package in the code execution sandbox but is completely unusable'.

signals.topic: SSE streaming hang detection: SDK silently drops ping events causing false-positive watchdog aborts in downstream clients
signals.summary: The SDK's streaming layer silently drops SSE ping events (`if (sse.event === 'ping') continue`), making it impossible for any downstream consumer (including Claude Code CLI) to distinguish 'server actively thinking' from 'stream silently stalled'. This causes false-positive watchdog timeouts during extended model thinking (Opus deep reasoning can be silent 60-120s between text deltas), producing hard errors like 'Stream idle timeout - partial response received' with no recovery path.
signals.review_reason: This is a high-frequency (cross-repo 40+ reports in Claude Code #46987 alone, plus multiple linked issues in the SDK) main-flow-blocking issue. Users experience hard crashes with no recovery path: 'Stream idle timeout - partial response received' errors that are unrecoverable without process restart. The root cause is confirmed in SDK source code (ping events silently dropped). Both issue #867 (real production hang, 0% CPU process, lost work) and #998 (40+ upstream reports + detailed root cause) provide strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Ping-aware streaming watchdog (fixes #749, #867, and downstream Claude Code hangs)
source_issues.evidence: Comprehensive proposal citing #749 (11 months open), #867, and upstream Claude Code #46987 (40+ reports in 24h). Documents the ping-drop site in src/core/streaming.ts lines 78-84. Provides reverse-engineered cli.js watchdog code and real log traces showing 3 consecutive 90s aborts on the same conversation. Ping events confirmed as being silently consumed by the SDK, with zero user-facing liveness signal.

source_issues.title: bug/proposal: infinitely hanging clients breaking bigger/complex sessions. Proposal: add Streaming Idle Timeout to Prevent Indefinite Hangs
source_issues.evidence: Real production session trace (f35c7c15-802e-462b-b468-b000a96e40bb) showing Claude Opus 4.5 stream stalled mid-stream with stop_reason:null, both processes stuck at 0% CPU indefinitely. Existing timeouts (overall timeout, AbortController, TCP keepalive) all failed. Documents the exact SSE event timeline of a real hang and explains why no existing mechanism detects it.

signals.topic: JSON parsing crashes when model outputs strings with invalid JSON escape sequences (e.g. regex literals, PHP namespaces, Windows paths)
signals.summary: When Claude generates JSON containing strings with invalid JSON escape sequences — such as regex patterns (\d, \p, \s), PHP namespaces (App\Http), or Windows paths — the streaming JSON parser crashes with an unhandled SyntaxError that crashes the entire Node.js process. Two separate code paths are affected: the main MessageStream parser and the partial-json-parser vendor library used for structured output.
aliases: JSON parse crash on regex escapes
signals.review_reason: Two independent issue reports confirm the same root cause: model output containing invalid JSON escape sequences crashes the streaming pipeline. Issue #996 shows the crash in the main parser with an unhandled SyntaxError (Node.js process crash). Issue #986 shows the same class of crash in the partial-json-parser vendor library used for structured output. Both have concrete reproduction paths. This blocks any workflow where Claude generates JSON with technical content containing backslashes (regex, file paths, LaTeX, etc.), a common use case for SDK users.

source_issues.title: bug(streaming): JSON.parse crashes on invalid escape sequences in model output
source_issues.evidence: Provides a concrete reproduction: asking the model to return a JSON object with a regex \\d+\\.\\d+ pattern triggers unhandled SyntaxError that crashes the Node.js process. Explicitly mentions the crash location as MessageStream.parse and the unhandled nature of the error.

source_issues.title: partialParse in _vendor/partial-json-parser crashes on invalid JSON escape sequences from model output
source_issues.evidence: Documents a second crash path in _vendor/partial-json-parser/parser.mjs when model outputs PHP namespaces with backslashes (App\Http\Middleware). Error 'Bad escaped character in JSON' thrown during input_json_delta accumulation at MessageStream line 501, killing the entire streaming response. Root cause traced to generate() not sanitizing string values before outputting to JSON string context.

signals.topic: toolRunner fails to propagate container.id across iterations causing either hard API errors or infinite tool call loops
signals.summary: When using client-side betaTools alongside code_execution_20260120 in a streaming toolRunner loop, the container.id is not forwarded from one iteration to the next. Both available workarounds are broken: passing a container object causes an API type error ('must be string'), while passing the string directly corrupts the accumulated message history and causes an infinite duplicate tool call loop. There is currently no working path to use betaTools with code execution in streaming mode.
aliases: infinite tool call loop in toolRunner
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed blocking bug in a core feature (toolRunner with code_execution). The compound failure means: (1) basic usage fails with a hard API error about missing container_id, and (2) the only available workaround fails in a worse way — creating an infinite loop with no exit path. This completely blocks any user trying to combine betaTools with code execution in streaming mode. Labeled 'bug' by the reporter, with full reproduction code and explicit 'no working path' statement.

source_issues.title: Bug: `toolRunner` does not propagate `container.id` across iterations, and `setMessagesParams` causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction code provided. After first iteration, iterationMessage.container.id exists but the next request omits it, causing API error 'container_id is required when there are pending tool uses generated by code execution with tools'. The setMessagesParams workaround either throws a type mismatch error (object vs string) or corrupts message history causing the model to repeatedly call code_execution+betaTool with identical inputs indefinitely. No working path exists for this use case. Environment: SDK 0.80.0, Node 22.14.0, claude-opus-4-6 / claude-sonnet-4-6.

signals.topic: Error propagation destroys ProcessError context — subprocess stderr/exit_code stripped, generic Exception raised
signals.summary: When the CLI subprocess exits non-zero, ProcessError is flattened through the message reader, losing exit_code and stderr. Users catch generic Exception with hardcoded 'Check stderr output for details' — CI/CD pipelines and concurrent setups cannot diagnose failures.
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn autonomous sessions destroyed on first recoverable API error (429). The SDK controls request cadence and has access to Retry-After headers yet treats transient rate limits as fatal. Three independent runs crashed identically; ~$2.50 in wasted API costs per failure. Makes standard-tier Console usage impossible for autonomous agents without manual intervention.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: ProcessError destroyed during propagation; stderr='Check stderr output for details' (hardcoded literal, never actual stderr); raised as bare Exception; isinstance(exc, ProcessError) always False; isinstance(exc, ClaudeSDKError) never fires in consumer code

source_issues.title: Error context destroyed through exception flattening — CLI failures produce unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1'
source_issues.evidence: Same triple defect: ProcessError with hardcoded stderr, str(e) flattening, bare Exception re-raise. Prevents ClaudeSDKError from firing in consumer code. Windows 11 confirmed, multiple users affected.

signals.topic: setting_sources=[] (empty list) silently ignored due to Python truthiness bug — all settings load regardless
signals.summary: ClaudeAgentOptions(setting_sources=[]) has no effect because the SDK checks the list with a truthiness test (if self._options.setting_sources:). An empty list is falsy in Python, so --setting-sources is never passed to the CLI, and all setting sources load including unwanted account-level MCP integrations. Same bug class as the fixed allowed_tools=[] bug.
aliases: all settings loaded despite empty list
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same bug. Empty setting_sources=[], which users expect to mean 'load no sources', is silently ignored and all sources load instead. This causes unexpected account-level MCP integrations to activate in SDK context, potentially triggering unwanted tool calls and billing. Simple fix available (is not None check) but bug remains unfixed.

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] (empty list) silently ignored — global settings always loaded
source_issues.evidence: Empty list [] is falsy → --setting-sources never passed to CLI → all setting sources load. Workaround: use setting_sources=[''] (truthy). Same class of bug as allowed_tools=[] fix #634.

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] silently ignored due to truthiness check in _build_command
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed same bug: line 283 uses 'if self._options.setting_sources:' instead of 'is not None'. Workaround requires passing [''] to force the flag. SDK 0.1.45 on Python 3.14.

signals.topic: Agent SDK crashes on 429 rate limit instead of backing off and retrying — destroys multi-turn agent sessions
signals.summary: The SDK raises a fatal exception on 429 rate limit responses rather than reading Retry-After and retrying. Multi-turn autonomous sessions that took 10+ minutes are completely destroyed, losing all progress. Makes autonomous agents unusable on standard Console tier (30k tokens/min limit).
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn autonomous sessions destroyed on first recoverable API error (429). The SDK controls request cadence and has access to Retry-After headers yet treats transient rate limits as fatal. Three independent runs crashed identically; ~$2.50 in wasted API costs per failure. Makes standard-tier Console usage impossible for autonomous agents without manual intervention.

source_issues.title: Agent SDK should handle 429 rate limits gracefully instead of crashing
source_issues.evidence: SDK crashes with fatal exception on 429. Multi-turn session destroyed, all progress lost. 3 independent runs crashed identically at same point. ~$2.50 wasted per failure vs ~$0.50 for a successful run. Standard Console tier (30k tokens/min) unusable for autonomous agents.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on every normal query() completion — 100% CPU until process restart
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport uses anyio.create_task_group() for stderr reading with manual __aenter__/__aexit__. On normal query() completion, close() is called from asyncgen finalizer task (not the original consumer task), triggering cross-task cancel_scope.cancel(). This pins one CPU core at 100% indefinitely per completed agent. Fires deterministically on every normal completion.
signals.review_reason: Fires deterministically on every normal query() completion. The anyio cancel scope affinity bug causes cross-task cancellation from the asyncgen finalizer task, leaving the scope in an inconsistent state. anyio's _deliver_cancellation reschedules itself via call_soon on every event loop tick, pinning one CPU core at 100% for the remaining process lifetime. This is a main workflow blocker for any sustained agent session — every completed agent leaves the process in a degraded state.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic on every normal async for query() completion. Cross-task cancel_scope.cancel() + __aexit__ from asyncgen_athrow task cancels original consumer. anyio _deliver_cancellation spins at 100% CPU on one core per completed agent until process restart. Verified: 4+ consecutive completions with diagnostic tracebacks showing Task-<N> coro=async_generator_athrow triggering the leak.

signals.topic: continue_conversation=True fails to resume previous session — always creates new session_id
signals.summary: When ClaudeAgentOptions(continue_conversation=True) is used, the SDK should resume the most recent session in the directory. Instead, a new session_id is created on every script run, making multi-turn session continuity impossible.
signals.review_reason: continue_conversation=True is a documented feature that is functionally broken. The session is not resumed across script runs, defeating the purpose of session continuity for multi-turn agent workflows. The feature makes persistent agent sessions impossible to implement.

source_issues.title: continue_conversation=True starts a new session instead of resuming the previous one
source_issues.evidence: Same script, same cwd, same SDK options. First run: session_id=A. Second run: session_id=B (new). Expected: second run resumes session A. Documented behavior of continue_conversation=True is broken.

signals.topic: outputFormat API returns subtype 'success' with undefined structured_output for complex JSON schemas, silently failing structured output

aliases: outputFormat silently fails on complex schemas

Users relying on structured output for data pipelines receive undefined values with a 'success' subtype, causing downstream logic to fail silently. The model correctly produces JSON but the SDK extraction/validation layer breaks for any non-trivial schema.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent — should return error_max_structured_output_retries

All failing cases (nested objects, $ref, deep schemas) return subtype: 'success' — never error_max_structured_output_retries. Model produces correct JSON in text but SDK doesn't extract it.

signals.topic: Plugin initialization times out with 'Control request timeout: initialize' in SDK 0.1.45+, blocking plugin usage

aliases: control protocol timeout during plugin init
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash that completely blocks plugin functionality for any user on SDK 0.1.45+. The plugin initialization path hits a hardcoded 65-second timeout and throws an unhandled exception. Given the regression from 0.1.44 to 0.1.45 across a 12-version range, this is a confirmed regression in the control protocol handshake that makes plugin-based workflows entirely unusable.

source_issues.title: Plugin initialization fails with 'Control request timeout: initialize' error in claude-agent-sdk versions 0.1.45 and above
source_issues.evidence: Timeout occurs at exactly 65 seconds (hardcoded timeout in _send_control_request). Affects SDK versions 0.1.45-0.1.56. Version 0.1.44 works. Full stack trace provided showing the timeout originates from anyio.fail_after() in the control protocol initialization phase.

source_issues.title: When calling the SDK in Docker, the following error occurs: 'Claude Code process exited with code 1'

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: zombie bun server processes spin at 100% CPU indefinitely on macOS/Linux
signals.summary: The orphan watchdog in telegram plugin v0.0.5 fails to detect dead MCP sessions because PPID-based detection is broken: the immediate parent is a bun wrapper that never changes PPID, so all three detection paths (PPID check, stdin.destroyed, stdin.readableEnded) silently fail. The MCP StdioServerTransport spins on a dead stdin pipe at ~98-100% CPU per zombie process, consuming CPU and heating machines indefinitely. Issue #1384 confirms the same behavior persists even after the v0.0.5 fix — the busy-loop inside the poller itself is never addressed.
aliases: orphan watchdog blind spot macOS Linux
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports confirm zombie bun processes consuming 98-100% CPU indefinitely on macOS/Linux. This is resource exhaustion (direct cost impact), machine heating, and indefinite process leakage — a clear main-flow blocking issue. PPID-based orphan detection has a systemic blind spot that silently fails.

source_issues.title: telegram: orphan watchdog ineffective -- zombie bun processes spin at 100% CPU
source_issues.evidence: Two zombie bun processes observed consuming ~98% CPU for 23h and 4h respectively, machine heating significantly. All three detection paths in watchdog fail silently.

source_issues.title: telegram: server.ts pegs 100% CPU per zombie poller despite 0.0.5 fix (#1349)
source_issues.evidence: Zombie processes at 94.8-98.6% CPU confirmed on both v0.0.4 and v0.0.5 builds. SIGTERM ignored, SIGKILL required to clear them.

source_issues.title: telegram: server.ts pegs 100% CPU per zombie poller despite 0.0.5 fix (#1349)

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: orphan watchdog false positives and signal handling failures on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, the orphan watchdog in telegram plugin v0.0.5 produces false positives: process.stdin.destroyed and stdin.readableEnded are unreliable under bun when the parent Claude Code CLI is busy, causing the MCP subprocess to self-terminate during normal long-running operations. Additionally, when the plugin tries to kill stale pollers, SIGTERM does not reliably terminate bun.exe processes on Windows, leaving stale pollers alive and causing 409 Conflict errors for new sessions. The bot.pid SIGTERM mechanism also kills the MCP pipe entirely on dual-load, taking the channel completely offline.
aliases: telegram orphan watchdog false positive Windows
SIGTERM doesn't kill bun on Windows
bot.pid SIGTERM kills MCP pipe dual-load
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports covering distinct Windows failure modes in the telegram plugin: orphan watchdog false positive (disconnects during normal use), SIGTERM ineffective (stale pollers persist causing 409 conflicts), and bot.pid SIGTERM killing MCP pipe (complete offline). All are Windows-platform-specific blocking issues that prevent reliable telegram plugin usage on Windows.

source_issues.title: [telegram] MCP subprocess self-terminates on Windows during long parent activity (orphan watchdog false positive)

source_issues.title: Telegram 0.0.5: bot.pid SIGTERM kills MCP pipe on dual-load -- acquireLock is safer
source_issues.evidence: When Claude Code dual-loads the telegram plugin, the bot.pid mechanism sends SIGTERM to the first bun process, killing the MCP pipe entirely and taking the telegram channel completely offline.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: inbound messages not delivered to Claude Code (poll loop exits prematurely)
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin's poll loop permanently exits on any transient error other than HTTP 409 Conflict. Connection timeouts, TLS resets, DNS hiccups, and HTTP 5xx errors cause the catch block to log 'polling failed' and return, exiting the loop permanently. The plugin process stays alive (MCP stdin keeps event loop running), so outbound Claude→Telegram tools work — but the bot becomes completely deaf to inbound messages. Users see the bot running but silently ignoring all incoming Telegram messages.
aliases: telegram inbound messages not reaching Claude Code
poll loop exits on non-409 errors
signals.review_reason: Two reports confirm that the core bidirectional messaging use case is broken: inbound Telegram→Claude direction silently fails while outbound direction works. This is not a minor degradation — it breaks the primary communication channel of the plugin. Count=2 below P0 threshold, so P1 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin 0.0.5: inbound messages not bridged to Claude Code (outbound works)
source_issues.evidence: Plugin consumes messages from Telegram API but they never reach Claude Code's input stream. Outbound reply tool works fine, confirming plugin process alive but deaf to inbound.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): poll loop exits permanently on non-409 errors -- root cause of 'inbound stops' reports
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: catch block exits loop on any non-409 transient error. Plugin process alive but poll loop dead, so only outbound works.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin v0.0.5: stale-poller kills legitimate concurrent sessions instead of only orphans
signals.summary: The bot.pid-based stale-poller reclaim logic in v0.0.5 is too aggressive: it sends SIGTERM to any process whose PID appears in bot.pid, without distinguishing between an orphaned zombie and a legitimate long-lived concurrent session. Legitimate concurrent sessions are killed, breaking active user sessions. Additionally, on upgrade from v0.0.4 to v0.0.5, the mechanism cannot detect v0.0.4 buns (which never wrote bot.pid), so both versions fight for the same bot token with no resolution.
aliases: stale-poller SIGTERM kills legitimate concurrent sessions
bot.pid migration blind spot v0.0.4 to v0.0.5
signals.review_reason: Two related reports confirm the v0.0.5 stale-poller regression kills active user sessions and fails to handle upgrades from v0.0.4. This breaks concurrent session support and upgrade paths — significant UX impact. Count=2 so P1, not P0.

source_issues.title: telegram v0.0.5: stale-poller SIGTERM kills legitimate concurrent sessions (regression from #1075 fix)

source_issues.evidence: v0.0.4 never wrote bot.pid, so on upgrade to v0.0.5 the stale-poller cannot detect the v0.0.4 bun. Both versions race for the same bot token, causing 409 conflicts with no resolution.

signals.topic: security-guidance hook outputs plain text instead of JSON, causing hook validation errors and blocking tools
signals.summary: The security-guidance plugin's PreToolUse hook outputs plain text to stderr and exits with code 2 when blocking, but Claude Code's hook system requires JSON format output. This causes 'hook json output validation failed' errors and prevents the security-guidance plugin from functioning. Additionally, even when functioning as designed, exit(2) blocks the tool instead of warning and proceeding, which contradicts the 'reminder' branding — users expect a warning, not a block.
signals.review_reason: Two reports covering the same hook's output format problem and its behavioral consequence (block vs warn). The hook is completely non-functional due to JSON validation errors, blocking the security-guidance plugin entirely. Combined impact makes this P1 despite count=2.

signals.topic: Windows平台下对话接口HTTP 500：Path.resolve()触发os.getcwd()与langgraph dev的blockbuster冲突

aliases: PDF upload 504 on sandbox cold start

signals.topic: Agent permanently stuck in 'Thinking' state due to terminal execution promise deadlock
signals.summary: Agent hangs permanently in 'Thinking' state when terminal commands exit before the user responds to 'Proceed While Running' UI. The flushBuffer ask() promise deadlocks because process completion does not resolve the pending response. Root cause in CommandOrchestrator flushBuffer interacting with Task.ask().
aliases: command marked as Skipped agent hangs
signals.review_reason: 2 tickets confirm the agent gets permanently stuck in Thinking state, blocking the main workflow. Issue #10235 provides deep technical root cause analysis identifying the exact deadlock in flushBuffer ask(). Issue #10208 shows the issue occurs with both cloud and local models, indicating broad impact.

signals.topic: Terminal output not captured in Docker containers after VSCode update — 'Terminal output not available' blocks agent commands
signals.summary: After VSCode 1.115.0, running terminal commands via Continue inside Docker containers (Dev Containers) no longer captures output. The command executes but Continue displays 'Terminal output not available', breaking all terminal-dependent agent workflows in containerized environments.
aliases: terminal capture fails in Docker containers
signals.review_reason: Terminal capture is essential for agent commands in containerized dev environments. The 'Terminal output not available' message indicates a complete capture failure, not a partial degradation. Linked to similar WSL regression (#9731), suggesting a systematic VSCode remote/workspace detection bug introduced in 1.115.0. Blocks all terminal-dependent workflows in Docker dev environments.

source_issues.title: Terminal output not captured in Docker container after VSCode update
source_issues.evidence: Command executes but output is not captured; Continue shows 'Terminal output not available'. Related to similar issues #9731 (WSL) and PR #9679, indicating a regression in remote/container environments introduced by VSCode 1.115.0.

signals.topic: crewAI uninstallable on Intel Macs due to mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency with no macOS x86_64 wheels
signals.summary: Intel Mac users cannot install crewAI at all because lancedb dropped x86_64 wheel support at 0.29.2, yet pyproject.toml declares it a mandatory core dependency. Full ResolutionImpossible error on pip/uv install.
aliases: lancedb dependency blocks macOS x86_64 install
cannot install crewai on Intel Macs
signals.review_reason: Complete installation blockage for Intel Mac users is a main-flow-blocking issue. Users cannot even pip install the product. The evidence is unambiguous: full uv resolution output, pyproject.toml smoking gun pinpointing lancedb as mandatory, and the fact that lancedb simply does not ship x86_64 macOS wheels at 0.29.2+. This is not an edge case — it affects every Intel Mac user trying to install crewai.

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: Author provides complete uv diagnostic output showing ResolutionImpossible error. Root cause: lib/crewai/pyproject.toml line 44 declares lancedb>=0.29.2 as a mandatory core dependency. lancedb dropped macOS x86_64 wheel builds at 0.29.2, making crewai uninstallable on all Intel Macs regardless of whether memory features are used. Available wheels listed: manylinux, macosx_11_0_arm64, win_amd64 only.

signals.topic: Google abuse detection blocks legitimate users during authentication, causing sign-in failures and tool lockout

One is a paying subscriber explicitly stating 'I can't access the thing I paid for.' This is a direct revenue-impacting blocker with no graceful error handling — the CLI dumps raw HTML into the terminal instead of explaining the issue or offering remediation.

signals.review_reason: Root cause is precisely identified (bundled xdg-open in 'open' npm package vs system xdg-open), the fix is known but unimplemented, and the user cannot complete authentication as a direct result. This is a complete auth flow blocker on Linux.

signals.topic: RipGrep download failure causes 2+ minute startup delay, severely degrading user experience

signals.review_reason: Maintained by a project maintainer, clearly scoped. While 2+ minutes of startup delay is not a crash, it is a significant experience degradation that affects every startup attempt on network-restricted machines. The issue has 'workstream-rollup' label indicating it is a tracked engineering priority.

source_issues.evidence: Maintainer-filed issue (jacob314) explicitly acknowledges the problem: 'Failing to download RipGrep causes 2+ minute wait even when the issue is just access to github.' Proposal includes bundling RipGrep (~10MB) to prevent the issue entirely.

signals.topic: WebSearchTool HTTP timeout is hardcoded to 30s and not configurable, causing ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs
signals.summary: WebSearchTool hardcodes timeout=30 on all HTTP requests with no user-configurable override. In corporate proxy and slow network environments, legitimate requests exceed 30s, causing ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs. Users must subclass or monkey-patch to adjust.
signals.review_reason: Issue #2162 documents hardcoded 30s HTTP timeout in WebSearchTool causing ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs in real corporate proxy and slow network environments. This is a direct workflow-blocking issue: the agent cannot complete its task, and there is no workaround available to users without subclassing or monkey-patching. The hardcoded timeout was introduced in PR #2140 and the new Exa backend has no timeout at all (PR #2139), meaning the pattern is inconsistent across backends. This satisfies the 'user impact evidence' bar: it causes repeated workflow failures and no user-configurable escape hatch exists.

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly describes ReadTimeout errors aborting agent runs in real corporate proxy/slow network scenarios, with no user override mechanism available.

aliases: web scraping blocked by Cloudflare in smolagents
signals.review_reason: Issue #2109 describes VisitWebpageTool silently failing on Cloudflare-protected sites, returning empty content on a 'large fraction' of useful URLs for research agents. While the issue is framed as a tool suggestion (anybrowse), it documents a real capability gap: web research agents silently produce incomplete or empty results with no error signal, which degrades output quality in a way users may not immediately diagnose. This qualifies as a user workflow issue with observable impact (empty content on real URLs), though it is not a total block since agents can continue running with degraded context.

source_issues.title: Tool suggestion: anybrowse for web scraping with Cloudflare bypass
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states VisitWebpageTool fails on Cloudflare-protected sites, silently returning empty content on a large fraction of useful URLs for research agents.
