aliases: Deploy bundler missing deps for 10 of 16 model providers
together provider not bundled — ImportError at runtime
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow failure for agent deployment. 10 of 16 supported model providers are affected. Deploy silently succeeds (exit 0) but the bundled agent crashes immediately on startup with ImportError. Users have no warning during the deploy flow and lose trust in the deployment tooling. Count=3 distinct issues across GitHub confirms this is a recurring, well-understood problem, not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: Deploy bundler missing deps for 10 of 16 model providers — silent ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: fireworks, together, deepseek, xai, nvidia, cohere, openrouter, perplexity, azure_openai, baseten all pass config validation, deploy exits 0, then runtime ImportError crashes the agent. Affected 10 of 16 providers.

source_issues.title: fix(deploy): bundler missing deps for 10 model providers — ImportError on deploy
source_issues.evidence: Detailed table of all 10 missing provider deps. Reproducer with fireworks model causes ImportError after deploy exits 0.

source_issues.title: deploy: together provider not bundled — ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Specific repro for together provider: deploy validates TOGETHER_API_KEY, exits 0, generated pyproject.toml missing langchain-together, agent crashes on start.

signals.topic: arxiv-search skill CLI entry point discards query_arxiv return value — script exits 0 with zero output despite documented behavior
signals.summary: The arxiv-search skill's main() calls query_arxiv() but drops the return value without printing it. The script exits 0 with no stdout or stderr, making the documented CLI completely unusable.
aliases: arxiv-search skill CLI produces no output
signals.review_reason: The CLI is documented to return paper titles and abstracts but silently produces zero output. This is a key-function breakage for the skill's CLI entry point — the user runs the command, gets no results, and has no indication of success or failure. With 530 installs, this is a real user-facing tool that is broken as documented.

source_issues.title: arxiv-search skill: CLI produces no output (main() drops query_arxiv return value)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 'uv run --with arxiv python libs/cli/examples/skills/arxiv-search/arxiv_search.py "transformer attention" --max-papers 3' — exits 0, zero stdout, zero stderr. SKILL.md documents it returns title+abstract but CLI never prints anything. 530 installs reported via npx skills.

signals.topic: PatchToolCallsMiddleware does not handle invalid_tool_calls — causes 400 BadRequestError blocking agent invocation with DeepSeek (token overflow/truncation)
signals.summary: When output token overflow causes JSON truncation, DeepSeek returns invalid_tool_calls. PatchToolCallsMiddleware only iterates msg.tool_calls, missing invalid_tool_calls, causing a 400 error: 'An assistant message with tool_calls must be followed by tool messages'. Agent invocation is blocked.
aliases: PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle msg.invalid_tool_calls without ToolMessage
signals.review_reason: This blocks the main agent invocation flow when using DeepSeek (and likely other non-OpenAI-compatible APIs) with output token overflow. The 400 error prevents the agent from completing any task. While count=1, the root cause is clearly identified, the fix is a one-liner, and the issue directly blocks the core agent.invoke() workflow — making it a genuine user pain point.

source_issues.title: PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle msg.invalid_tool_calls without ToolMessage
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: DeepSeek model with token overflow/truncation produces invalid_tool_calls. Middleware only checks msg.tool_calls, misses invalid_tool_calls. Causes BadRequestError 400 'An assistant message with tool_calls must be followed by tool messages'. Verified fix in source code. Present in latest commit.

signals.topic: GET /threads/{thread_id}/history throws ValueError: Subgraph tools not found — breaks conversation history retrieval
signals.summary: When retrieving thread history via the REST API, deepagents fails with ValueError: Subgraph tools not found because the 'tools' subgraph is written to checkpoints but not properly exposed via aget_subgraphs() to the LangGraph runtime.
aliases: Subgraph tools not found when calling /threads/{thread_id}/history
signals.review_reason: Thread history retrieval is a core feature for resuming conversations. The ValueError makes this entire API endpoint unusable for any agent using custom tools. While count=1, the failure is deterministic (not environment-specific) and breaks a primary workflow: users cannot inspect or resume conversation history after tool use.

source_issues.title: Subgraph tools not found when calling /threads/{thread_id}/history
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: (1) create agent with custom @tool, (2) run one conversation to create checkpoint, (3) call GET /threads/{thread_id}/history → ValueError: Subgraph tools not found at langgraph/pregel/main.py:1436 in aget_state_history. Root cause: deepagents compiles tool execution into named 'tools' subgraph written to checkpoint but doesn't expose it via aget_subgraphs().

signals.topic: Tool call parser crashes on malformed function dicts, silently drops ALL valid tool calls
signals.summary: default_tool_parser and default_tool_chunk_parser crash with unhandled TypeError/KeyError when a raw tool call has a malformed function field (None or empty dict). The outer caller catches Exception broadly, causing ALL tool calls in the same batch — including perfectly valid ones — to be silently dropped from agent execution.
signals.review_reason: Agent tool-calling is a core workflow. When a single malformed function dict appears in a streamed response, the entire parsing loop throws an unhandled exception. The outer caller catches Exception broadly, causing ALL tool calls (including perfectly valid ones in the same batch) to be silently dropped. This is a silent data loss bug in the critical path of agentic execution.

source_issues.title: core: default_tool_parser crashes on malformed function dicts, silently drops all valid tool calls
source_issues.evidence: default_tool_parser and default_tool_chunk_parser crash with TypeError/KeyError when function field is malformed. The caller catches Exception broadly, so ALL tool calls (including valid ones) are silently dropped. Repro: passing function=None or empty function dict crashes the entire parsing loop.

signals.topic: Streaming tool_call chunks with same index split into blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
signals.summary: When a provider emits multiple same-index tool-call fragments within a single streamed AIMessageChunk, AIMessageChunk.init_tool_calls() incorrectly produces a blank tool_call (empty name/args) and moves the real call into invalid_tool_calls. Valid LLM-generated tool calls are silently discarded and never executed.
aliases: same-index tool call fragments cause blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
streaming tool call chunk merging bug
signals.review_reason: Tool calling via streaming is a primary agent workflow. When a provider emits multiple same-index fragments in one delta, the real tool call is incorrectly placed into invalid_tool_calls and replaced with a blank tool_call. This means valid LLM-generated tool calls are silently discarded and never executed — a silent failure in the agentic execution path.

source_issues.title: bug(core): same-index tool_call chunks in one streamed delta can split into blank tool_calls and invalid_tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: When a provider emits multiple same-index tool-call fragments within a single streamed delta, init_tool_calls() produces a blank tool_call (empty name/args) and moves the real call into invalid_tool_calls. Real provider payloads trigger this. Reproduction shows output: tool_calls=[{name:'', args:{}, id:null}], invalid_tool_calls=[{name:'search', args:'...', id:'id1'}].

signals.topic: _batch(0, iterable) causes infinite loop; _abatch(0, iterable) yields empty batches indefinitely
signals.summary: The langchain_core.indexing._batch and _abatch utilities lack input validation for batch_size. Passing size=0 causes _batch to enter an infinite loop (process hang = complete blocking) and _abatch to yield empty batches forever (silent performance degradation and wasted CPU). These functions power the core aindex/index document ingestion API.
aliases: batch_size=0 causes process hang and async empty batch flood
indexing batch utilities lack input validation
signals.review_reason: The indexing API (aindex/index) is used for document ingestion pipelines — a core production workflow. Passing batch_size=0 (a simple config mistake) causes synchronous calls to hang indefinitely (process hang = complete flow block) and async calls to silently flood with empty batches (wasted CPU, no progress). No validation exists to fail fast, making this a dangerous input validation gap in a core API.

source_issues.title: bug(core): _batch and _abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop
source_issues.evidence: _batch(0, [1,2,3]) enters an infinite loop — while True never exits because islice(it, 0) returns empty list indefinitely. _abatch(0, async_iter([1,2,3])) yields empty lists forever, causing silent performance degradation and wasted CPU. These functions are used by langchain_core.indexing.aindex and index.

signals.topic: _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
signals.summary: When OpenAI's service_tier (priority/flex) is used and the API response omits cached_tokens in prompt_tokens_details, _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'int' and 'NoneType'. This breaks cost tracking for all responses using these pricing tiers.
aliases: service_tier token arithmetic crashes on None cached_tokens
usage metadata computation crash with priority/flex tier
signals.review_reason: Usage metadata tracking is essential for cost monitoring and billing reconciliation in production deployments. When a user enables OpenAI's service_tier (priority/flex) on a response that doesn't include cached_tokens, the usage metadata computation crashes the entire call. This means cost tracking breaks for all responses using these pricing tiers, directly impacting billing accuracy.

source_issues.title: bug(openai): _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
source_issues.evidence: Calling _create_usage_metadata with service_tier='priority' and prompt_tokens_details={} raises TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'int' and 'NoneType'. The dict stores None for missing cached_tokens, and .get(key, 0) returns None because the key exists with value None.

signals.topic: ShellSession.execute() times out incorrectly when command stdout has no trailing newline
signals.summary: ShellSession injects a completion marker using a separate printf call. When a command's stdout lacks a trailing newline, the marker is appended to the same line. The current startswith(marker) detection fails, causing the session to incorrectly mark the command as timed out even though it completed successfully.
aliases: ShellSession completion marker detection fails without trailing newline
shell tool timeout on no-newline output
signals.review_reason: ShellSession is a production tool for executing commands via agents. When a command produces output without a trailing newline (common in printf, file content reads), the completion marker detection fails and the command is incorrectly marked as timed out. This causes valid shell commands to be treated as failures — a false negative in a core execution path. Count=1 so P2.

source_issues.title: ShellSession times out when stdout has no trailing newline and the done marker is appended to the same line
source_issues.evidence: ShellSession.execute() injects a completion marker using a separate printf call. When the command's output lacks a trailing newline, the marker is appended to the same line. The current startswith(marker) check misses it, causing the command to time out incorrectly. Repro: printf 'hello without newline' returns timed_out=True, output='', exit_code=None.

signals.topic: push_message crashes with UnboundLocalError when callbacks is None
signals.summary: The push_message() function in langgraph/graph/message.py fails to initialize the 'handlers' variable when config['callbacks'] is None (the default). This causes an UnboundLocalError at runtime, blocking the core message handling path used by all agents.
signals.review_reason: UnboundLocalError is a runtime crash that blocks the core message handling path. It occurs with the default config (callbacks=None) which is the most common usage pattern. Two independent reports confirm this is a real user-blocking issue. Count=2 is below P0 threshold but the crash nature warrants P1.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message when callbacks is None or unexpected type
source_issues.evidence: Calling push_message(HumanMessage(content='test', id='msg-1')) raises UnboundLocalError: local variable 'handlers' referenced before assignment when config['callbacks'] is None (the default). The handlers variable is only assigned in if/elif branches, never initialized for the None case.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message and dead code in _strip_extras
source_issues.evidence: Same UnboundLocalError in push_message: handlers variable only assigned inside if/elif branches for BaseCallbackManager or list of BaseCallbackHandler. When config['callbacks'] is None, neither branch executes and handlers is undefined at line 360.

signals.topic: _strip_extras dead code fails to unwrap Required/NotRequired types
signals.summary: The _strip_extras() function in langgraph/channels/binop.py has unreachable code that should unwrap Required/NotRequired wrapper types, but the check order causes it to always take the wrong branch, silently producing incorrect type unwrapping for annotated Required types.
signals.review_reason: Dead code in a core channel utility causes silent incorrect behavior for Required/NotRequired type handling. Two independent reports confirm this is a code defect affecting state channel type processing. Not P0 due to count=2 and no evidence of main flow blockage.

source_issues.title: Bug: _strip_extras has unreachable code, fails to unwrap Required/NotRequired types
source_issues.evidence: Line 26 (Required/NotRequired check) is unreachable dead code because line 24 (general __origin__ check) always executes first. For Required[Annotated[int, ...]], the wrong branch executes, producing incorrect type unwrapping.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message and dead code in _strip_extras
source_issues.evidence: Same dead code issue: _strip_extras returns Required (the origin) instead of int (the wrapped type) for Required[int]. The Required/NotRequired check comes after the general __origin__ check which catches everything first.

signals.topic: langgraph-cli 0.4.21 missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
signals.summary: langgraph-cli 0.4.21 imports typing_extensions in schemas.py but does not declare it as a package dependency, causing ModuleNotFoundError in clean environments like GitHub Actions runners immediately on installation.
signals.review_reason: Missing dependency causes complete CLI failure on first use in clean environments (CI/CD pipelines, new containers). This is a packaging defect introduced in 0.4.21 that blocks the langgraph-cli main entry point. Count=1 but P1 due to clear blocking evidence and common CI/CD use case.

source_issues.title: langgraph-cli 0.4.21: Missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner: pip install langgraph-cli==0.4.21 followed by langgraph build crashes with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typing_extensions'. Verified by comparing v0.4.19 (no import) vs v0.4.21 (imports typing_extensions in schemas.py line 3). Workaround: manually pip install typing_extensions.

signals.topic: Long tool calls silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud after ~180s causing duplicate work and 2-3x cost multiplication
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud (EU, Plus tier), tool calls taking longer than ~180 seconds are silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both complete successfully, causing 2-3x redundant LLM calls and cost. This is reproducible and consistent across langgraph 1.1.3 through 1.1.6.
aliases: tool call silent re-execution LangGraph Cloud
long tool calls duplicate execution ~180 seconds
signals.review_reason: Silent duplicate execution of long tool calls on managed cloud causes 2-3x cost multiplication with no user indication. This directly wastes LLM tokens and API costs. Clear reproduction evidence across multiple versions. P1 (not P0) because count=1 and the issue is specific to the managed cloud platform.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible on managed LangGraph Cloud: at ~180s after a long tool call starts, duplicate runs appear in the trace with identical tool call arguments and their own tools node but no preceding model node (not triggered by LLM). Both original and duplicate complete successfully, causing 2-3x redundant work. Consistent across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6, EU Cloud, Plus tier. BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 is hardcoded. Related to #6726 (CancelledError not caught) and #5672 (run cancellation loses un-checkpointed state).

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresSaver threading.Lock serializes async operations causing 75% throughput loss in high-concurrency deployments
signals.summary: AsyncPostgresSaver uses an instance-level threading.Lock() across its async cursor methods (get_tuple, put), serializing all concurrent asyncio tasks. In a 500-user concurrent load test, this produced 199 req/s vs 1295 req/s for raw psycopg_pool — a 6x throughput difference and 10x latency increase.
signals.review_reason: threading.Lock in async code creates a severe throughput bottleneck (6x loss) and 10x latency increase in production deployments. This is a major cost and performance issue for high-concurrency deployments. Clear benchmark evidence from a 500-user load test confirms the impact.

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresSaver enforces instance-level threading.Lock() during asynchronous execution
source_issues.evidence: 500-user concurrent load test on GKE + Cloud SQL PostgreSQL with max_size=100: AsyncPostgresSaver throughput 199 req/s avg 1923ms latency vs raw psycopg_pool baseline 1295 req/s avg 88ms latency. Python threading.Lock() in async context serializes all concurrent tasks, blocking psycopg_pool from utilizing its 100-connection pool.

signals.topic: Dify Cloud new user OAuth sign-in blocked by 500 error
signals.summary: New users cannot complete Google/GitHub sign-in on Dify Cloud. After OAuth authorization, the callback returns 500 Internal Server Error, preventing new user registration entirely.
signals.review_reason: New user registration on Dify Cloud is completely blocked for OAuth providers (Google/GitHub). This is a critical auth regression impacting all new users trying to sign up, with a clear reproduction path and 500 error evidence. Severity: P0 — registration is a primary entry point.

source_issues.title: Dify Cloud v1.13.3: new users cannot sign in via Google or GitHub after OAuth callback (500 Internal Server Error)
source_issues.evidence: New users cannot sign in using Google or GitHub on Dify Cloud. After completing OAuth authorization, callback returns 500 Internal Server Error. Existing registered users can still log in; only new users are affected. Reproduction: choose Continue with Google/GitHub, complete authorization, observe redirect/callback returns {"message":"Internal Server Error","code":"unknown","status":500}.

signals.topic: Qdrant vector database batch delete fails with 500 Internal Server Error on large document sets

source_issues.title: qdrant delete items is so large lead server error

signals.review_reason: Users cannot use the OpenClaw Mem0 plugin at all after initial setup because it enters an infinite startup failure loop on every restart. Even if the field is manually removed, the plugin re-writes it, creating a permanent block.

signals.topic: AG-UI protocol: state not passed to AgentSession and internal API blocking multi-agent orchestrations
signals.summary: AG-UI fails to pass state (agent_id, user_id, tenant_id) to AgentSession, breaking ContextProviders. Additionally, all AG-UI conversion API types are internal, preventing multi-agent orchestrations from using the protocol.
aliases: AG-UI ContextProvider cannot receive context info
cannot merge multi-agent streams to AG-UI SSE
signals.review_reason: AG-UI protocol is broken on two fronts: ContextProviders cannot receive agent_id/user_id/tenant_id via AG-UI, blocking authentication and personalization; and the AG-UI conversion API is internal, preventing multi-agent orchestrations from using AG-UI for CopilotKit compatibility. Together these block enterprise multi-agent production scenarios.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: The current implementation of AG-UI fails to pass the state to AgentSession
source_issues.evidence: AG-UI protocol fails to pass state to AgentSession. ContextProvider relies on state to transmit agent_id, user_id, tenant_id but these cannot be passed when using AG-UI protocol, breaking authentication and personalization.

source_issues.title: .NET: Make AG-UI conversion API public for multi-agent orchestrations
source_issues.evidence: All AG-UI conversion machinery (BaseEvent, AsAGUIEventStreamAsync, AGUIServerSentEventsResult) is internal. Multi-agent swarm orchestrator cannot merge per-agent streams into single AG-UI SSE stream without reimplementing the protocol from scratch.

after_run providers fire on streaming errors

source_issues.evidence: After_run context providers (session persistence, audit logging) are invoked after a streaming failure instead of only on success. Affects all agents using AgentTelemetryLayer. Side effects run on error responses, causing data corruption and incorrect audit trails.

signals.topic: CosmosCheckpointStorage bypasses RestrictedUnpickler, breaking security model parity with FileCheckpointStorage

signals.review_reason: Security and correctness issue: CosmosCheckpointStorage bypasses the RestrictedUnpickler security model that FileCheckpointStorage enforces. Users who switch storage backends unknowingly accept different security postures with no migration warning, creating production risk.

source_issues.title: Python: Add allowed_checkpoint_types support to CosmosCheckpointStorage for parity with FileCheckpointStorage
source_issues.evidence: CosmosCheckpointStorage passes raw bytes to pickle.loads instead of using RestrictedUnpickler like FileCheckpointStorage does. Users switching between storage backends face security and behavior differences with no warning.

signals.topic: Web scraping agents fail on Cloudflare-protected sites, blocking research tasks
signals.summary: AutoGen agents performing web research are blocked by Cloudflare bot protection on ~60% of high-value web targets (news, LinkedIn, Amazon, government sites), returning 403 errors or empty content. This is an active operational failure for research agents with no built-in workaround in the framework.
aliases: web scraping failure on protected sites
bot detection blocking agent research tasks
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete, ongoing operational failure: research agents in production cannot reliably fetch from a majority of meaningful web targets. The issue clearly describes a workflow-blocking problem (403 errors) affecting a specific agent use case (web research), with no workaround currently in AutoGen. While only 1 issue is captured, the 60% failure rate on high-value targets represents significant impact on core functionality.

source_issues.title: Tool suggestion: anybrowse for MCP-native web scraping with Cloudflare bypass
source_issues.evidence: AutoGen agents doing web research hit a common wall: Cloudflare-protected sites return 403s or empty content. Standard HTTP fetchers don't work on ~60% of high-value web targets.

signals.topic: AutoGen Studio lacks i18n support, excluding non-English developers from the UI
signals.summary: AutoGen Studio has all ~143 UI strings hardcoded in English across ~30 React components, creating a significant usability barrier for the Chinese developer community and other non-English speakers who make up a large portion of the AutoGen user base.
aliases: no Chinese language support in AutoGen Studio
hardcoded English UI excludes non-English developers
signals.review_reason: While technically a feature request, the hardcoded English-only UI creates a persistent exclusion barrier for a substantial portion of the user base. The Chinese developer community is explicitly called out as a large user segment unable to use AutoGen Studio's UI effectively. This falls under 'experience significant degradation' for a specific user segment. Count is 1 so priority is P2 rather than P1.

source_issues.title: Feature: Add Internationalization (i18n) Support to AutoGen Studio
source_issues.evidence: AutoGen Studio currently has all UI text hardcoded in English across ~30 React components (~143 translatable strings). This creates a significant barrier for non-English-speaking developers, especially the large and growing Chinese developer community.

signals.topic: page.request.get() does not send context cookies, breaking authenticated API testing
signals.summary: When using page.request.get() (or other APIRequestContext methods), cookies from the current browser context are not automatically sent with the request. Users must manually extract and inject cookies via headers as a workaround, which is error-prone and blocks automated workflows that rely on session-authenticated API calls.
aliases: cookies not sent with API requests
signals.review_reason: User impact is clear: automated authenticated API testing is broken. Workaround requires manual cookie extraction per request, which is error-prone and blocks CI workflows relying on session cookies.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Context cookies not sent when using page.request.get()
source_issues.evidence: User must manually extract cookies and inject Cookie header: await page.context().cookies(url); then manually build header. No automatic cookie propagation from browser context to API requests.

signals.topic: HTML report viewer breaks when report.js bundle contains literal </script> sequence
signals.summary: When the Playwright HTML reporter inlines report.js into index.html, any literal </script> string in the bundle (e.g. from React innerHTML calls) causes the browser to prematurely close the script tag. The report page renders raw JavaScript text instead of the UI, making the report completely unreadable.
aliases: HTML report shows raw JS instead of UI
report viewer broken inline script injection
signals.review_reason: Critical workflow blocker: the HTML report viewer is completely unusable when </script> appears in the bundled report.js. This breaks the primary post-test analysis workflow for any test run that triggers such content (e.g., React-based apps).

source_issues.title: HTML report breaks when inlined report.js contains </script>
source_issues.evidence: Browser terminates script block early due to literal </script> in bundle. The page at localhost:9323 displays raw JavaScript instead of report UI. Workaround requires PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_DO_NOT_INLINE_ASSETS=1.

signals.topic: clock.install() patches setTimeout in transient iframes causing NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED and blank pages
signals.summary: Since v1.57.0, clock.install() patches setTimeout in every frame via addInitScript. Third-party libraries like Sentry that create temporary iframes to obtain native function references end up with dead references after those iframes are destroyed. Calling the cached Playwright wrapper throws NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED synchronously, which React's error boundary catches and responds to by unmounting the app — resulting in a blank page.
aliases: setTimeout wrapper causes iframe reference error
signals.review_reason: This is a real-world app-breaking regression. In production-like scenarios using popular libraries like Sentry, clock.install() causes blank pages via a synchronous error caught by React error boundaries. The regression was introduced in v1.57 and persists.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: clock.install() patches setTimeout in transient iframes — cached references throw NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED in Firefox
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression from 1.56.1 to 1.57.0. Real-world breakage: Sentry Replay's debounced flush triggers React DOM commits, React try/catch catches the NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED, error boundary unmounts app resulting in blank page.

signals.topic: playwright-cli kill-all does not kill daemons due to pattern case mismatch and dead patterns
signals.summary: The playwright-cli kill-all command greps ps aux for daemon process patterns. The pattern 'cli-daemon' (hyphenated) never matches because running daemons use 'cliDaemon' (camelCase). Additionally, 'run-mcp-server' and 'run-cli-server' are dead patterns left over from a previous architecture. As a result, kill-all silently fails to kill any daemon processes, forcing users to manually find and kill them.
signals.review_reason: A core maintenance command (kill-all) is completely broken and silently fails to kill daemon processes. Users must manually find and kill daemons, causing resource leaks and confusion.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: playwright-cli kill-all does not kill daemons due to pattern mismatch in killAllDaemons
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: 'cli-daemon' vs 'cliDaemon' case mismatch and dead argv token patterns. Only 'dashboardApp.js' matches real processes. The kill-all command silently fails to kill any daemon.

signals.topic: Playwright CLI drag command throws Zod validation error and is completely non-functional
signals.summary: The playwright-cli drag command accepts element selectors as positional arguments but the CLI daemon converts them to startRef/endRef and never passes startElement/endElement to the MCP tool. This causes Zod to reject the undefined values with 'expected string, received undefined', making the drag command completely unusable.
aliases: CLI drag command broken validation error
signals.review_reason: A specific CLI feature (drag-and-drop) is completely non-functional due to a missing parameter in the MCP tool call chain. Users attempting to use the drag command encounter an immediate validation error with no workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright CLI Drag is not working
source_issues.evidence: Zod validation error: 'Invalid input: expected string, received undefined' for startElement and endElement. Root cause: daemon's drag command converts positional args to startRef/endRef but never passes startElement/endElement to MCP tool.

signals.topic: Kernel 缺少 agent tool execution 的审计追踪钩子，无法满足 EU AI Act 合规要求
signals.summary: Semantic Kernel 没有提供 pre/post function execution hook 来生成不可篡改的操作记录，导致金融、医疗等监管行业部署时无法满足 EU AI Act Article 12 的自动事件日志要求，也影响企业级审计能力。
aliases: missing audit trail hooks for agent actions
no tamper-evident records of function calls
EU AI Act Article 12 compliance gap
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue（#13851 和 #13813）均来自同一用户，明确指出监管合规缺口：EU AI Act Article 12 要求不可篡改的操作记录，但 SK 无 kernel-level hook，需 monkey-patching 才有变通方案。这是关键功能缺失而非功能请求——金融/医疗监管部署因此无法合规使用 SK，属于可验证的用户痛点。count=2 但两个 issue 实为同一用户分两次提交，置信度略降。优先级 P2（count 不足以 P0，且为合规缺失而非主流程阻断）。

source_issues.title: Audit trail hooks for agent tool execution
source_issues.evidence: 明确指出 EU AI Act Article 12 要求可独立验证的自动事件日志；指出 LangChain/PydanticAI/CrewAI 均已有此模式；提出 kernel-level pre/post function execution hook 方案；已关闭并有1条评论

source_issues.title: Audit trail for plugin/function calls
source_issues.evidence: 描述金融和医疗部署场景下审计是 table stakes；描述需要 'signature over (agent_id, function_name, inputs, outputs, timestamp)'；指出当前需 monkey-patching；已关闭并有1条评论

signals.topic: Chat/Completions API not supporting reasoning models (no reasoning output)
signals.summary: 用户调用 chat/completions API 时，reasoning 内容完全不输出。LLM 生成了 reasoning 但 SK 无法将其传递给用户，导致关键模型能力完全不可用。
aliases: reasoning models not working in chat completion
signals.review_reason: 用户痛点明确：reasoning 模型的核心输出（thinking/reasoning content）完全不显示，等同于关键模型能力不可用，直接阻断需要 reasoning 的使用场景。count=1 单例但有截图证据，属于高置信度 bug，优先级 P1。

source_issues.title: Bug: chat/completions no reasoning
source_issues.evidence: 截图显示 reasoning 内容完全缺失，主流程阻断；标签为 bug，状态 open，用户提供了完整复现截图

signals.topic: ChatCompletion usage 对象仅返回最后一次 LLM 调用的 token 统计，多轮对话计费数据严重失真
signals.summary: 执行多轮对话或连续 function calling 时，usage 对象只记录最后一次 API 调用的 token 消耗，导致企业无法准确核算每个客户的真实用量，造成计费/成本核算系统性错误。
aliases: usage object incomplete for multiple LLM calls
token accounting wrong across multiple calls
ChatCompletion usage only reflects last call
signals.review_reason: 这是企业级计费阻断 bug：多轮对话或连续 function calling 时 token 统计仅记录最后一次调用，导致企业成本核算系统性错误。11 条评论证明多个用户受影响，issue 明确指出'proper token accounting per customer, it is a must'——这不是边缘问题，而是生产级计费准确性破坏，符合 P0 高频主流程阻断（有明确复现场景）。count=1 但影响极端（计费失真），review_reason 给出强用户影响证据。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Chatcompletion usage object reflects only last LLM call even when multiple has been made
source_issues.evidence: issue 标题明确描述多 LLM 调用时 usage 仅返回最后一次；11 条评论表明多个用户受影响；issue 正文明确说明 'proper accounting of tokens spend per customer, it is a must'，将计费影响定性为企业级硬需求；平台 NuGet 1.54.0 版本可复现

signals.topic: Python 端 Kernel 缺少跨插件共享计算结果的能力，导致相同 embedding 重复生成
signals.summary: 用户在不同插件中需要对同一输入 query 做 embedding，但 SK Python 版无法在 kernel 层面传递预计算的中间结果，导致每个插件重复调用 embedding 服务，产生不必要的延迟和成本浪费。
aliases: no shared context for pre-computed embeddings
signals.review_reason: 用户体验明确：跨插件无法共享预计算的 embedding 结果，导致重复调用 embedding 服务，直接造成延迟和成本浪费。这是 SK Python 端的设计缺失，影响使用向量索引的多插件场景用户，5 条评论进一步证明非单例问题。标记为 P1（主流程体验下降，非阻断但影响效率）。

source_issues.title: Python: What is the alternative to Kernel.Data in C# within python implementation
source_issues.evidence: 用户描述在不同插件中重复对同一 query 做 embedding，'the same operation is being performed within each plugin, causing duplicate calls to my embedding generation service'；提出明确使用场景（多插件从向量索引检索 search documents/images）；5条评论表明有其他用户遇到同类问题

signals.topic: VS Code extension file link regression: all file reference links (absolute, relative, workspace) broken after April update
signals.summary: VS Code 扩展中 Codex 生成的所有本地文件链接（绝对路径、相对路径、工作区相对路径、带行号锚点）全部失效，用户无法点击跳转到引用文件，4月更新后引入回归。
signals.review_reason: 三条 issue 共同描述 Codex 核心使用场景——点击引用文件跳转——在4月更新后大规模失效。#17649 是明确标记为 regression 的全格式链路断裂，影响所有 Windows VS Code 用户；#17682/#17681 分别是空格路径失效和行号锚点失效，同一根本功能的不同维度退化。高频（count=3）、主流程阻断（文件导航是 Codex 最核心的差异化能力之一），有三组独立样例链接支撑，P0 无疑。

source_issues.title: [regression] Any links (file references) in the VS Code extension chat are not working
source_issues.evidence: Regression after April update; user tested all link formats (absolute, workspace-relative, file://, #L anchors) and none work; user considering switching to other solutions; references prior unaddressed issues #16117, #17334.

source_issues.title: Codex app can't open clickable local file paths when the path contains spaces (macOS)
source_issues.evidence: File paths with spaces render with % encoding but clicking produces no action or 'Unable to load file' on macOS.

source_issues.title: Desktop app code hyperlinks open the file but do not navigate to the referenced line
source_issues.evidence: Line-number anchors (line 868, line 1099) open the correct file but never navigate to the referenced line; reproduced with multiple links.

signals.topic: CLI permission system fails to persist file edit approvals and reject compound commands, rendering Codex unusable
signals.summary: 用户在 CLI 中选择「不再询问」后文件编辑权限仍被反复索取；复合命令（&&拼接）即使子命令已授权也会被沙箱拒绝；用户明确反映该系统不可用，一名用户已因此取消订阅。
signals.review_reason: 两条 issue 均来自真实付费用户（'most expensive' 订阅），明确描述权限系统核心功能失效：持久化授权不生效（issue #17668，直接导致退订）；复合命令审批体系与模型行为不兼容（issue #17670）。两条均有具体操作路径和错误现象，不属于功能请求或路线图讨论，是影响主流程阻断的用户痛点。

source_issues.title: Permissions system doesn't support compound commands
source_issues.evidence: User reports permissions system is unusable with the model; compound commands with individually approved sub-commands are rejected by the harness.

source_issues.title: Persisting approvals for file edits does not work
source_issues.evidence: User chose 'yes, and don't ask for this file ever again' but still gets prompted; user cancelled $200/month subscription and states Codex is unusable.

signals.topic: Windows desktop app session/UI state corruption: unexpected new thread creation during generation and stale branch indicators
signals.summary: Windows 桌面应用中，活跃会话生成过程中 UI 异常切换到新线程；分支指示器频繁显示过期或缺失的值；这两类 UI 状态错误导致用户在关键工作流中迷失。
signals.review_reason: #17661 和 #17683 虽为不同现象但根因相近：Windows 桌面应用 UI 对 session/git 状态的维护不稳定。#17661 发生在模型生成期间，UI 自动跳转导致当前工作丢失；#17683 则是 git 工作树场景下的分支状态过期。两者均反映 Windows app 在活跃开发会话中的状态完整性问题，对用户工作流造成明确干扰，属于体验显著下降。

source_issues.title: Codex opens NEW CHAT without me doing anything
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows with PRO subscription reports app intermittently navigates away from active generating thread to a blank new thread with no user input; reproducible intermittently.

source_issues.title: branch indicator often stale or missing
source_issues.evidence: User with pre-created git worktrees reports branch indicator shows stale branch or nothing at all when starting a new thread; user must manually select correct branch each time.

signals.topic: Incorrect billing/usage limit display: users observe unexpected quota consumption and vanished refresh timers
signals.summary: 用户报告订阅额度被异常消耗（周额度凭空消失约一半）、5小时刷新计时器不显示、刷新时间被莫名推迟，属于计费异常的用户痛点。
signals.review_reason: 两条 issue 均描述用户实际额度与系统显示不符：#17651 明确显示 43% 额度凭空消失，5小时刷新计时器消失，刷新时间被推迟；#17663 是 Business Plan 管理员使用 2/5 席位仍被限流。两者均为可感知的计费异常，且有截图证据支撑（#17651），属于明显成本损失类痛点。

source_issues.title: reach my limits
source_issues.evidence: Business Plan admin with 5 seats using only 2 still told limit reached after 20-30 min; repeated contact with admin unable to resolve; clear quota management bug.

source_issues.title: Half of my weekly limit just vanished.
source_issues.evidence: User at 80% weekly limit observes 43% of quota suddenly vanishes with no corresponding activity; 5-hour refresh timer disappeared; weekly reset postponed by days; explicit 'please fix' request with screenshot evidence.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox firewall setup fails with SetRemotePorts HRESULT(0x80070057), blocking application startup
signals.summary: Windows 版 Codex 在启动时沙箱防火墙配置失败，SetRemotePorts 因 NET_FW_IP_PROTOCOL_ANY + 无端口条件组合被 Windows Firewall COM 拒绝，导致沙箱规则未创建，工具执行路径被阻断。
aliases: Windows firewall COM error during sandbox setup
sandbox firewall rule creation fails on Windows
signals.review_reason: 虽然是单条 issue，但用户提供了详尽的本地调试证据（6步复现路径、sandbox.log 截取、Windows Firewall COM 行为验证），明确指向 codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/firewall.rs 中 ensure_offline_outbound_block() 的实现 bug。该 bug 导致沙箱设置关键路径失败，Codex 无法以安全模式运行，属于主流程阻断。Enterprise 订阅用户，排除纯安全公告，应保留。

source_issues.title: Windows app sandbox setup fails with SetRemotePorts failed (HRESULT(0x80070057)) when building outbound firewall rule
source_issues.evidence: Enterprise PRO user on Windows 11; sandbox setup path (windowsSandbox/setupStart) fails; loopback rules created but outbound block rule absent; user traced root cause to ensure_offline_outbound_block() with Protocol=Any + no remote ports + SetRemotePorts call; user confirms fix direction.

signals.topic: Conversation sanitizer strips required 'id' field from built-in tool-call items causing 400 API errors
signals.summary: When using OpenAIConversationsSession with FileSearchTool, CodeInterpreterTool, or WebSearchTool, the internal sanitizer removes the required 'id' field from these item types, causing the Conversations API to return 400 Missing required parameter errors on turn 2+. All three built-in tool types are affected (file_search_call, code_interpreter_call, web_search_call). This is a complete session workflow blocker for agents using these tools.
aliases: sanitizer strips required id from tool call items
id field stripped from built-in tool items
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed workflow blocker: FileSearchTool, CodeInterpreterTool, and WebSearchTool all produce items with required 'id' fields, but the sanitizer unconditionally removes them, causing a 400 error on any follow-up turn. The root cause is precisely identified (line 568 of session_persistence.py), reproducible steps are given, and there is a known workaround (custom sanitizer). This blocks the main use case of OpenAIConversationsSession with built-in tools.

source_issues.title: _sanitize_openai_conversation_item strips required id from built-in tool-call items
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed 400 error on OpenAI API when FileSearchTool is used with OpenAIConversationsSession. The sanitizer in session_persistence.py line 568 unconditionally strips 'id' from all items, but the API requires id on file_search_call, code_interpreter_call, and web_search_call item types.

signals.topic: Eager sqlite3 import causes deployment failures on restricted Python environments
signals.summary: The agents package imports sqlite3 at module load time, which causes import-time failures on Google Cloud Run and other minimal Python images where sqlite3 is not available. Users must manually specify a custom base image with sqlite3, causing unexpected deployment downtime.
aliases: sqlite3 not available in Cloud Run
Google Cloud Run deployment failure agents package
signals.review_reason: Deployment failure on a major cloud platform (Google Cloud Run) is a clear user pain point. The issue is reproducible and has a significant operational impact: the user's server was down for an hour. While the author frames it as an enhancement request, the effect is a deployment-breaking bug for any user on restricted Python environments. The workaround of changing base image is non-obvious and imposes hidden operational cost.

source_issues.title: Don't eagerly import sqlite3
source_issues.evidence: User reports deployment failure on Google Cloud Run due to sqlite3 not being present in the default Python image. User had a down server for an hour while working around the issue. Workaround requires modifying deployment config to use a full Python image. This is a deployment-blocking issue for any user targeting minimal/cloud environments.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError导致multiprocess forkserver worker中请求大规模失败
signals.summary: 使用pydantic 2.12+与DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD时，在multiprocess forkserver环境下，0.6%~9.5%的请求因PydanticUserError失败，生产环境大规模受影响
signals.review_reason: 明确的用户影响证据：生产级别multiprocess环境中0.6%~9.5%的请求失败率，且随时间增长。在高并发fork模式下失败被缓存导致worker级联全量失败，主流程严重阻断，属于关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: 在multiprocess forkserver(~700 workers, 数百万请求规模)下：DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true时~0.6%错误率且随时间增长；DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false时~9.5%错误率，且失败被缓存后该worker所有请求全部失败

signals.topic: AsyncCompletions.parse()动态Pydantic模型导致内存无限增长
signals.summary: 使用response_format传入create_model动态生成的Pydantic模型时，内存持续增长无上限，可能导致长时运行进程OOM
signals.review_reason: 明确的内存泄漏证据：动态Pydantic模型配合parse()导致gc无法回收，内存无上限增长。在长时运行的AI agent或服务中会逐渐耗尽内存导致崩溃，属于资源泄漏导致的流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Possible memory leak in `AsyncCompletions.parse()`
source_issues.evidence: 使用create_model动态生成Pydantic模型传入response_format后，gc.collect()后内存仍持续增长，监控gc.get_objects()数量持续上升，长时间运行将导致OOM，影响所有使用parse()进行结构化输出的长时进程

signals.topic: Responses API在tool-call-only轮次中不触发server-side compaction
signals.summary: 使用context_management compaction时，纯tool_call输出的轮次不产生compaction事件，导致上下文无限增长直至context_length_exceeded，tool-heavy agent循环被阻断
aliases: Server-side compaction missing on function_call turns
Responses API compaction not emitted in tool-only turns
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Responses API的核心compaction特性在tool-call-only场景下完全不触发，导致上下文无限膨胀直至触发context_length_exceeded。严重影响tool-use agent开发场景，是Responses API的主要工作流阻断问题。

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: tool-heavy agent循环中所有轮次均只返回function_call时，response.output中无compaction事件，input_tokens持续从5084→5119→5154增长，最终将触发context_length_exceeded，Responses API的关键compaction功能完全失效

signals.topic: 使用自定义API base URL时请求被静默拦截
signals.summary: 使用自定义base_url(如Azure、代理)时，所有请求返回OpenAIException 'Your request was blocked'，SDK行为与直接HTTP请求不一致
aliases: Request blocked with custom API base
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：使用自定义API base是常见部署模式(Azure、代理、第三方兼容端点)，SDK在此场景下请求完全失败，但requests库直连同地址成功，说明SDK引入了导致阻断的额外逻辑，阻止了大量企业级部署方案。

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – "Your request was blocked" with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: 使用自定义base URL时所有请求返回'Your request was blocked'，但相同请求用requests库直接发起成功，说明SDK在某处(请求头/拦截器)引入了额外校验导致请求被阻断，影响所有使用代理/Azure/自定义端点的场景

signals.topic: ACP device pairing/approval fails under reverse proxy with path-based routing
signals.summary: When OpenClaw ACP is reverse-proxied by Caddy (or similar) with a path after the domain (e.g., /openclaw), the ACP device pairing/approval flow breaks. Devices appear as pending but `devices approve all` fails with "unknown requestId", and the ACP client connection fails with "pairing required".
aliases: ACP pairing fails behind reverse proxy
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker. The user cannot complete the ACP device pairing and approval flow when using a reverse proxy with path-based routing, which is a common deployment pattern. The errors 'unknown requestId' and 'pairing required' completely prevent the intended ACP client-to-server connection. Single issue but with extremely clear and concrete user impact evidence (exact error messages, reproduction steps, stack traces).

source_issues.title: Connect to another OpenClaw via ACP issue
source_issues.evidence: User set up Caddy reverse proxy with basePath '/openclaw'. Pending device appears in `devices list` but `devices approve all` throws `GatewayClientRequestError: unknown requestId`. ACP client connection throws `GatewayClientRequestError: pairing required`. Both operations are completely blocked.

signals.topic: acpx claude exec fails with 'Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto' preventing Claude sessions from starting
signals.summary: Running `acpx claude exec` (or spawning via sessions_spawn with runtime='acp') immediately fails with Internal error because the ACP SDK sends `permissions.defaultMode: 'auto'` in the session/new request, but claude-agent-acp only accepts specific values like 'bypassPermissions', 'acceptEdits', etc.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core use case of spawning Claude sessions via acpx. The user cannot start a Claude exec session at all — it fails immediately with an Internal error. A viable workaround exists (use Claude CLI directly) but that defeats the purpose of using acpx as the agent runtime layer.

source_issues.title: claude exec fails with 'Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto' - session/new sends unsupported defaultMode
source_issues.evidence: acpx claude exec fails immediately with Internal error. Verbose output shows: 'Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto'. The session/new JSON-RPC request contains permissions.defaultMode: 'auto' which claude-agent-acp rejects. User is forced to bypass acpx and use Claude Code CLI directly as workaround.

signals.topic: Persistent session resumption fails because sessionDir field is always null
signals.summary: When creating a persistent session with `acpx <agent> -s <name> exec`, the session appears in `status` and `sessions` commands but `prompt` fails with 'No acpx session found' because the sessionDir field in the session JSON index is null, preventing any follow-up prompts to existing sessions.
aliases: sessionDir null causes prompt to fail
signals.review_reason: This breaks the fundamental promise of persistent sessions — the ability to resume a conversation with a follow-up prompt. The session is created and tracked by the system but cannot be resumed, which is a complete workflow failure for any user relying on multi-turn sessions.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions: sessionDir is null, prompt cannot find session
source_issues.evidence: User creates persistent session with `acpx gemini -s test_session exec 'hello'`. `status` and `sessions` show the session exists. But `acpx gemini -s test_session prompt 'are you still there?'` fails with 'No acpx session found'. Root cause: sessionDir field in ~/.acpx/sessions/<uuid>.json is null. Core persistent session workflow (create, resume with prompt) is completely broken.

signals.topic: 安全扫描器将合法技能错误标记为可疑（VirusTotal误报导致用户无法正常发布）
signals.summary: ClawHub安全扫描系统（包含VirusTotal Code Insight）将多个功能合法、无恶意行为的技能标记为"Suspicious"，导致用户技能在市场上展示为可疑、无法正常分发，严重损害平台信任和开发者体验。
aliases: security scanner over-triggering on benign skills
skill flagged as suspicious false positive
signals.review_reason: 这是高频(count=8)、跨多类技能的系统性问题。多个开发者上传功能完全合法（本地记忆管理、支付SDK、风险检查、持久化记忆）的开源技能，被ClawHub安全扫描系统或VirusTotal Code Insight标记为'Suspicious'，导致技能在市场上展示异常，直接阻断新开发者正常发布流程。OpenClaw自身扫描器多次正确识别为'Benign'但被VirusTotal结论覆盖，说明平台存在安全判定优先级问题。每一个issue均有具体技能URL和代码证据，用户体验下降明确。部分用户（如session-memory-context作者）是平台新用户，首次发布即遭阻断，影响严重。

source_issues.title: 我的SKILL被误认为可疑
source_issues.evidence: 技能使用官方lark-cli API和飞书官方API用法，却被标记为可疑，用户要求复核并说明原因。

source_issues.title: my skill got flagged when its safe
source_issues.evidence: 新用户首次发布技能即被标记为可疑，该技能仅做本地会话管理（session-memory-context），不执行外部脚本、不下载上传任何内容，被标记后用户无法正常分发并主动要求说明具体触发规则。

source_issues.title: False positive: bitfence flagged as suspicious by VirusTotal Code Insight
source_issues.evidence: BitFence是Solana/Base链上交易前风险检查工具（纯指令清单Manifest，无可执行代码），VirusTotal Code Insight因包含'transaction'/'wallet'/'USDC'等词将其误判为恶意，平台显示Suspicious导致用户信任受损。

source_issues.title: False positive: pay-skill flagged as suspicious by VirusTotal Code Insight
source_issues.evidence: pay-skill的x402支付协议核心功能（发HTTP请求获取402状态、发送USDC）被VirusTotal标记为'SSRF'和'敏感token'，OpenClaw自己的扫描器正确判定为Benign，但VirusTotal的误判导致平台显示Suspicious banner，用户困惑于哪个结果优先。

source_issues.title: False positive: rewind-memory flagged as Suspicious by VirusTotal
source_issues.evidence: rewind-memory持久记忆SDK（subprocess调用本地rewind CLI、auth_token引用用户配置文件），VirusTotal将其误判为Suspicious，OpenClaw自己的扫描器判定为Benign HIGH CONFIDENCE，两个系统结论矛盾。

source_issues.title: False positive: rewind-memory flagged as Suspicious by VirusTotal
source_issues.evidence: 同issue #1642，用户报告VirusTotal将'subprocess'、'auth_token'、'crypto'等关键词误判，OpenClaw扫描器判定Benign HIGH CONFIDENCE，但平台仍显示Suspicious flag。

source_issues.title: ClawHub Security flagged skill as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: 用户上传的技能被ClawHub Security标记为suspicious，用户不知具体原因，要求复核并说明如何解除标记。

source_issues.title: Appealing "Suspicious" flag on degausai/wonda (Wonda CLI skill)
source_issues.evidence: Wonda技能因使用Cookie认证（X/LinkedIn/Reddit用户自愿提供，本地存储，直发对应平台）被标记为'Suspicious'，用户认为应归为'elevated risk'而非'Suspicious'，强调这是该类工具的标准做法且完全开源可查；同时'curl|bash'安装模式也被误判为可疑。

signals.topic: 技能上传后无预警消失且账户无法重新登录
signals.summary: 用户上传技能后技能在约5分钟内自动消失，且无法重新登录账户，疑似平台自动 moderation 系统误操作导致用户内容丢失和账户被临时阻断。
aliases: 上传技能后消失且无法登录
signals.review_reason: 虽然count=1，但这是单一用户遭遇的严重阻断问题：技能消失（工作成果丢失）同时伴随无法登录（账户层面阻断），且用户完全不知道是 moderation 政策触发、安全扫描自动删除还是平台 bug，没有收到任何通知。技能用于银行核心Max的MCP通信，涉及巴西真实商业用户(Appmax)。虽然count低，但影响程度高（账户+内容双重阻断），属于关键功能不可用场景，应保留为P1。

source_issues.title: My skill just disappeared, and I can't log in again.
source_issues.evidence: 用户上传技能后5分钟技能消失且账户无法登录，用户明确提及'was my account affected or blocked'，技能和账户同时受影响，用户不知是平台自动删除还是账户被封禁，处于完全未知状态。

signals.topic: ClawHub MIME类型检测将.ts文件误判为video/mp2t导致TypeScript技能被标记为可疑
signals.summary: ClawHub安全扫描器将所有.src/*.ts文件错误识别为MIME类型video/mp2t（MPEG-2 Transport Stream），进而触发'suspicious patterns'警告，将正常的TypeScript编写的开源AWS SRE技能错误标记。
aliases: MIME type false positive for TypeScript files
.ts extension confusion with MPEG-2 Transport Stream
signals.review_reason: count=1，属于单一技术缺陷导致的误报。虽然影响范围较小，但根因清晰（ClawHub MIME检测逻辑缺陷：将.ts/.ts共享扩展名的TypeScript源代码误判为MPEG-2视频流），且已有明确的技术证据（6个文件均被标记为同一错误MIME类型），用户要求修改检测逻辑而非仅要求个案处理。如果不修复会影响所有TypeScript编写的技能，属于平台级bug而非个案。优先级降为P2是因为count低且主要影响TypeScript技能。

source_issues.title: False positive: openclaw-aws-sre-report flagged due to .ts MIME type misdetection (video/mp2t)
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确提供了clawhub inspect的原始输出，证明6个.ts文件均被标记为video/mp2t，skills使用TypeScript编写AWS SRE工具（CloudWatch/SQS/Cost Explorer/Bedrock），扫描器将视频流标记识别为'suspicious patterns'，用户提供了GitHub源码链接以证明完全开源合法，要求修正MIME检测逻辑。

signals.topic: Approval resume token invalid across separate tool calls — blocks async approval workflow
signals.summary: When a pipeline pauses at an approval gate and returns a resumeToken, using that token in a subsequent tool call fails with 'Invalid token' or 'Invalid pipeline resume state'. This directly breaks the async approval pattern, which is Lobster's core safety primitive. Users must fall back to avoiding approval gates entirely.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug with reproducible steps that directly blocks the core approval gate workflow — Lobster's primary safety primitive. The async approval pattern is completely broken: users cannot pause a workflow and resume it in a separate tool call. Workaround (avoiding approval gates) defeats the product's safety purpose. P0 despite count=1 because the impact is a hard block on a core feature with no acceptable workaround.

source_issues.title: lobster resume: token invalid across tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Bug with exact repro steps: pipeline with approval gate returns needs_approval + resumeToken; next tool call with lobster resume --token <token> --approve true returns 'Invalid token'. Same agent session, same gateway process. Workaround: avoid approval gates.

signals.topic: Approval gate pauses have no notification — workflows silently block with no user awareness
signals.summary: When a workflow reaches an approval gate and pauses, there is no notification mechanism. Users who are not watching the terminal never know a workflow is waiting. For async and background automations, this renders approval gates completely ineffective — workflows sit idle indefinitely with no signal to the user.
aliases: no alert when workflow waiting for approval
signals.review_reason: Approval gates are described as Lobster's 'core safety primitive' in the issue itself. Without notifications, paused workflows are completely invisible to users not actively monitoring the terminal, making the safety primitive effectively non-functional for any real-world async use case. This is a hard functional gap that defeats the purpose of the feature.

source_issues.title: feat: Notifications for paused approval gates
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states: 'If you are not actively watching the terminal, the workflow sits silently blocked indefinitely. This makes approval gates — Lobster's core safety primitive — impractical for any async or background automation.' The VISION.md shows a Telegram notification example that has no built-in implementation.

signals.topic: No dry-run mode — workflows must be tested in production, risking irreversible actions
signals.summary: There is no way to execute a workflow in safe mode. Workflows with write operations (HTTP POST, file deletion, git push) run live with no preview. A mistake in a workflow definition can cause real damage before any approval gate is reached, since approval gates themselves can be bypassed by editing the file mid-run.
aliases: cannot test workflow without running it
signals.review_reason: Absence of dry-run means write operations in workflows are untested in production. The issue directly acknowledges 'real damage' as a risk. Combined with the fact that workflow files can be edited mid-run (noted in #94), this creates a scenario where destructive steps can execute without any preview or safety net. P1 rather than P0 because damage is conditional on workflow content, not guaranteed.

source_issues.title: feat: Dry-run / safe mode for workflows
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states: 'your only option is to run it live and hope it behaves correctly. For workflows with irreversible side effects (sending emails, posting messages, creating cards, deleting files), a mistake in the workflow definition can cause real damage before any approval gate is reached.'

signals.topic: No per-step timeout — any hung step causes indefinite workflow hang with no recovery
signals.summary: Lobster provides no mechanism to set timeouts on individual steps. A hung curl, unresponsive LLM provider, or blocking shell script will hold the entire workflow forever. This is especially critical given Lobster's use case as an automation framework where LLM provider outages and network failures are routine.
aliases: workflow hangs indefinitely on slow step
no abort signal for hung steps
signals.review_reason: Without per-step timeouts, any network failure or provider outage causes the entire workflow to hang indefinitely. For an automation framework intended to run recurring workflows (e.g., 'every 5 minutes'), a single hung step can block all subsequent executions permanently. This is a reliability gap with concrete failure scenarios documented.

source_issues.title: Per-step timeout with on_error integration
source_issues.evidence: Issue lists concrete failure scenarios: 'LLM provider outages: llm.invoke to a degraded provider can hang for minutes', 'Network reliability: API calls without explicit -m flags wait indefinitely', 'Workflow SLAs: interactive triage workflows need bounded execution time.'

signals.topic: No on_error handling — any step failure halts entire workflow with no partial recovery
signals.summary: When any step fails in a Lobster workflow, the entire workflow halts with an unrecoverable error. There is no way to continue past a failed step, record the error, or let subsequent steps decide how to proceed. Multi-source monitoring, notification fan-out, and cleanup workflows cannot tolerate this behavior.
aliases: workflow halts on any step error
signals.review_reason: Total workflow halt on any step failure makes Lobster unsuitable for resilient automation scenarios. The described use cases (multi-source monitoring, fan-out notifications, cleanup workflows) are core automation patterns that cannot work when a single source failure stops everything. This directly impacts the reliability of multi-step workflows.

source_issues.title: Per-step on_error handling for partial failure recovery
source_issues.evidence: Issue describes concrete use cases that are impossible today: 'Multi-source monitoring: if one source is down, the dashboard update should still run with partial data'; 'Notification fan-out: send to Slack, email, and PagerDuty — if Slack is down, still send email'; 'Cleanup workflows: delete temp resources from 3 providers — one failure shouldn't prevent cleaning the others.'

signals.topic: Background exec, cron automation, and subagent announce workflows are all broken
signals.summary: Three separate issues affecting the core automation triad: background exec completion wake (66135), isolated cron exec dispatch (66142), and subagent announce routing (66158). All three directly block user-defined automated agent workflows — a documented main flow. The regression in 66135 has 100% reproduction rate and makes Claude Code agent runs undetectable automatically. Together they represent high-frequency impact on the platform's core scheduling and automation story.
aliases: cron exec tool calls not dispatched
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues affecting the core automation triad: background exec completion wake (66135), isolated cron exec dispatch (66142), and subagent announce routing (66158). All three directly block user-defined automated agent workflows — a documented main flow. The regression in 66135 has 100% reproduction rate and makes Claude Code agent runs undetectable automatically. Together they represent high-frequency impact on the platform's core scheduling and automation story.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Background exec exit does not wake session, cron --at jobs silently disappear, Claude CLI --print output truncated (since 2026.4.10)
source_issues.evidence: Background exec exit no longer wakes session (notifyOnExit broken since 2026.4.10), cron --at jobs silently vanish without firing, Claude CLI --print output truncated to last line only. 100% reproduction rate across 4 attempts. Blocks all automated agent workflows.

source_issues.title: Cron subagent announce doesn't inherit parent cron's delivery target channel
source_issues.evidence: Subagent completion announces route to main session's last active channel instead of the cron's configured delivery channel. Cron results flood the wrong channel. Common with workflow engines that spawn subagents.

source_issues.title: Isolated cron sessions do not execute exec tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Isolated cron sessions fire and receive messages but exec tool calls are never dispatched. Script execution silently fails with no log entries. Blocks all scheduled agent tasks requiring shell access.

signals.topic: exec host=node denies absolute-path binaries and macOS node shell commands are unusable
signals.summary: Two separate exec/node issues: absolute-path binaries denied on remote nodes even with fully open security policy, and macOS node advertises shell commands that fail to execute. These degrade node exec functionality but are not complete blocks since direct exec without host=node may still work.
signals.review_reason: Two separate exec/node issues: absolute-path binaries denied on remote nodes even with fully open security policy, and macOS node advertises shell commands that fail to execute. These degrade node exec functionality but are not complete blocks since direct exec without host=node may still work.

source_issues.title: exec host=node denies absolute-path binaries under security=full ask=off
source_issues.evidence: Absolute-path binaries like /bin/ls, /opt/homebrew/bin/gh, /usr/bin/python3 are denied with SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED even when exec policy is security=full ask=off. Interpeter-without-file case is rejected while same interpreter with file succeeds.

source_issues.title: macOS node advertises shell commands but node exec is unusable
source_issues.evidence: exec host=node fails with 'node does not support system.run.prepare'. system.which fails with missing data error. Node advertises shell commands that are not actually functional.

signals.topic: openclaw doctor hangs at 100% CPU with large agent configs, blocking system usability
signals.summary: openclaw doctor hang at 100% CPU is a complete block for any user with a multi-agent config. The system cannot be diagnosed, restarted, or used until per-agent model config is stripped. The root cause is well-identified (uncached disk reads in plugin auto-enable loop) and the workaround is confirmed. This is a main-flow-blocking crash that makes the system entirely unusable for large deployments.
signals.review_reason: openclaw doctor hang at 100% CPU is a complete block for any user with a multi-agent config.
