source_issues.title: [Bug]: openclaw doctor hangs at 100% CPU after Plugins step with large agents.list containing per-agent model overrides
source_issues.evidence: Hangs after Plugins step consuming 100% CPU indefinitely. Root cause: O(N^2) loop over auto-enable candidates calling uncached synchronous fs.readFileSync 3 times per iteration. Confirmed workaround with Map-based cache resolves hang. Blocks doctor and gateway restart entirely.

signals.topic: CLI memory commands crash with unknown embedding provider, blocking memory operations
signals.summary: Memory CLI commands (status, backup, rebuild) crash entirely for users who have configured ollama as their embedding provider. This is a complete block for memory operations via CLI while the gateway itself works fine. The root cause is clear: the CLI code path skips plugin loading so the ollama adapter is never registered.
aliases: memory embedding provider not found CLI
signals.review_reason: Memory CLI commands (status, backup, rebuild) crash entirely for users who have configured ollama as their embedding provider. This is a complete block for memory operations via CLI while the gateway itself works fine. The root cause is clear: the CLI code path skips plugin loading so the ollama adapter is never registered.

source_issues.title: CLI memory commands crash with 'Unknown memory embedding provider: ollama'
source_issues.evidence: openclaw memory status/backup/rebuild all crash with 'Unknown memory embedding provider: ollama'. CLI code path does not load plugins so ollama adapter is never registered. Gateway memory_search works fine — only CLI is broken. Blocks all memory CLI operations for users with provider='ollama'.

signals.topic: Managed loopback browser profile fails due to SSRF policy applied to own CDP endpoint
signals.summary: The managed browser profile completely fails to start when any SSRF strict mode is active, including the exact configuration the docs recommend. The gateway refuses to connect to its own Chrome process even though it is demonstrably running and reachable. This is a main-flow blocker for browser operations and a regression.
signals.review_reason: The managed browser profile completely fails to start when any SSRF strict mode is active, including the exact configuration the docs recommend. The gateway refuses to connect to its own Chrome process even though it is demonstrably running and reachable. This is a main-flow blocker for browser operations and a regression.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Managed loopback browser profile fails ensureBrowserAvailable because agent SSRF policy is applied to its own CDP endpoint
source_issues.evidence: Chrome is alive and CDP is reachable via curl, but OpenClaw refuses to connect to its own spawned Chrome. The agent-facing ssrfPolicy is incorrectly applied to internal gateway lifecycle probes. Any strict-mode SSRF config (including docs-recommended hostnameAllowlist) breaks the managed browser. Regression.

signals.topic: Desktop app 连接本地模型（Ollama/LMStudio）时出现 Path not found 错误
signals.summary: 桌面应用在配置 Ollama 或 LMStudio 本地模型时崩溃，提示 "Path not found"，而终端版本相同配置下正常工作。用户无法在桌面应用中与本地 AI 模型交互。
aliases: desktop app local model connection failure
desktop app lmstudio path not found
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 构成用户痛点：主流程阻断（桌面应用无法使用本地模型）、有清晰复现路径、截图佐证错误现象。虽然 count=1 不足以支撑 P0，但 'Path not found' 错误直接导致核心交互功能不可用，且 desktop app 与 terminal 版本行为不一致表明这是系统性问题而非用户配置错误，应保留为 P1 级别跟踪。

source_issues.title: Path not found when discuss with agent via Ollama/LMStudio in desktop app
source_issues.evidence: 桌面应用配置 Ollama 后点击 discuss 按钮触发 'Path not found' 错误，终端版本同样配置可正常工作。提供完整复现步骤（macOS Tahoe + Ollama serve + desktop app 0.4.3），6 条评论讨论解决方案。

signals.topic: Aider crashes on startup with uncaught TypeError/PermissionError in pathlib operations
signals.summary: Aider throws uncaught TypeError or PermissionError during pathlib operations on startup, preventing the application from launching. Users see raw Python tracebacks instead of a graceful error message.
signals.review_reason: 3 uncaught exceptions during startup (TypeError, PermissionError, OSError) directly prevent the application from launching. Users get raw Python tracebacks with no graceful degradation. The TypeError occurs when working tree dir is None, the PermissionError when the cache directory cannot be created. These are main-flow blocking bugs affecting every new installation or certain environment configurations.

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in pathlib.py line 373
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'NoneType'. Crashes in utils.safe_abs_path -> Path(res).resolve() during GitRepo init on startup.

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1311
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/app/.aider'. Crashes during version check mkdir on startup.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054
source_issues.evidence: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054, crash reported.

signals.topic: Aider crashes on Windows with UnicodeEncodeError when printing to cp1252 console
signals.summary: Aider crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on Windows when Rich console attempts to print Unicode block characters (\u2588) to a console using cp1252 encoding, which cannot encode those characters.
aliases: Rich console crash on Windows terminal
signals.review_reason: The UnicodeEncodeError is an uncaught crash that prevents Windows users from using Aider's core lint/warning output flow. The crash occurs inside Rich's console write pipeline when printing Unicode characters to a cp1252-encoded Windows terminal, blocking the main editing workflow. While count=1, the impact is a complete workflow block for affected Windows users.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u2588' in position 39 on Windows cp1252 console. Crashes during tool_warning output in send_message -> lint_edited flow. Affects Windows users with cp1252-encoded terminals.

signals.topic: Aider fails to create new files — tool creates file path but file is not actually created
signals.summary: When Aider determines a new file needs to be created, it prompts the user to add the file to the chat, but then immediately reports 'file not found' and drops the file. The file is never actually created on disk, breaking the core code generation workflow.
aliases: tool drops file because it was never created
signals.review_reason: This is a core functionality failure: Aider's file creation workflow is completely broken for the affected user. The tool decides to create a file, prompts for confirmation, then fails because the file doesn't exist — indicating the LLM's intent to create was never carried out. This blocks the primary use case of generating new code files.

source_issues.title: Aider not creating files
source_issues.evidence: User reports that Aider asks to add file, then says 'file not found' and drops the file. The directory is empty — the file was never created. Affects multiple model combinations on OpenRouter. The tool-level intent to create the file is expressed but the file is never written to disk, making the entire feature non-functional.

signals.topic: 'Don't ask again' (D) option in prompts does not persist across sessions
signals.summary: When Aider prompts the user with a Y/N/D question and the user selects 'D' (Don't ask again), the preference is not saved. The same question is asked again on every subsequent startup, making the feature non-functional.
aliases: Don't ask again preference not saved
D option in prompts doesn't persist
signals.review_reason: The 'Don't ask again' feature is broken — user preferences are not persisted, causing repeated interruptions on every startup. While not a crash, it causes significant UX friction and repeated interruptions for users with custom/unknown model configurations.

source_issues.title: "Don't ask again" does not work
source_issues.evidence: User selects 'D' (Don't ask again) for a model warning prompt, but the same question appears again on every startup. The preference is not being persisted to storage. Affects any unknown model configuration.

signals.topic: Aider crashes with ModuleNotFoundError when using web scraping feature without playwright installed
signals.summary: When a user attempts to scrape a URL using the /web command, Aider crashes with an uncaught ModuleNotFoundError because the playwright module is not installed, instead of providing a clear error message.
signals.review_reason: The web scraping feature crashes with an uncaught ModuleNotFoundError instead of gracefully informing the user that playwright needs to be installed. This causes an unexpected application exit when the feature is used without the optional dependency, breaking the web browsing workflow.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in scrape.py line 134
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright' occurs when user runs /web command to scrape a URL. The exception is not caught and crashes the application instead of displaying a helpful message about installing playwright.

signals.topic: Web UI eval runner crashes with circular JSON error when using LLM providers (Bedrock/Anthropic) as llm-rubric judge
signals.summary: When using any LLM provider (AWS Bedrock or Anthropic) as the judge for `llm-rubric` assertions via `defaultTest.options.provider`, running an eval from the web UI throws a circular JSON serialization error and the eval never executes. The same configuration works from CLI, meaning the entire web UI eval path is blocked for a core feature.
aliases: llm-rubric judge fails in web UI
signals.review_reason: Web UI is a primary interface for promptfoo users. The entire eval execution path is completely blocked when using a common configuration (LLM provider as judge). The eval never runs. This is a P0 despite count=1 because it represents complete failure of a core user-facing feature with clear reproduction steps and evidence.

source_issues.title: Converting circular structure to JSON when using Bedrock provider as llm-rubric judge in UI
source_issues.evidence: Web UI crashes with 'TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON' when using Bedrock or Anthropic provider as judge. Eval never executes in UI; same config works in CLI. Both AWS SDK and Anthropic SDK clients contain circular references that break JSON.stringify in the UI worker path.

signals.topic: promptfoo redteam discover command completely fails with HTTP 400 Unknown task error
signals.summary: `promptfoo redteam discover` fails with HTTP 400 on every request, returning 'Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery'. The same endpoint works for `redteam generate` (HTTP 200), meaning an entire red team workflow is completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: A named command in the red team toolchain is completely broken — fails 100% of requests with HTTP 400. This is a primary workflow failure for users relying on the discovery phase of red teaming. Evidence is unambiguous (identical request structure succeeds for a different task name).

source_issues.title: `promptfoo redteam discover` fails with `Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery`
source_issues.evidence: Command fails 100% of the time with HTTP 400. Debug logs show task name 'target-purpose-discovery' is rejected by the server while 'excessive-agency' works at the same endpoint with same credentials. Red team discovery workflow is entirely non-functional.

signals.topic: Provider config parameters leak across providers in multi-provider eval causing HTTP 403 failures
signals.summary: When running multiple OpenAI providers in a single eval, `max_tokens` from one provider's config leaks to other providers that don't set it. This causes HTTP 403 failures when mixing older models (that accept `max_tokens`) with newer models (that reject `max_tokens` and require `max_completion_tokens`). A properly-configured eval silently fails for some providers.
signals.review_reason: A core eval feature (multi-provider configuration) silently produces incorrect results — provider calls fail with HTTP 403 because config parameters leak across providers. Users running multi-provider comparisons get unexpected failures with no indication that the cause is config isolation. This is a correctness bug in a frequently-used feature.

source_issues.title: max_tokens config leaks across providers in multi-provider eval
source_issues.evidence: Setting max_tokens: 16000 on gpt-4.1-mini causes that parameter to be sent to gpt-5.4-mini API calls, resulting in HTTP 403. Provider configs are not isolated in multi-provider eval runs. Workaround requires running each provider as a separate eval.

signals.topic: G-Eval assertion silently fails with NaN score and empty reason when value is empty array
signals.summary: `handleGEval` produces NaN for both `score` and `pass` when `renderedValue` is an empty array. The assertion silently fails with no actionable feedback — users see FAIL with `score: NaN` and an empty reason string. The bug is caused by division by zero (0/0) when the inner loop never executes.
signals.review_reason: An assertion type produces silent false failures with no actionable feedback (NaN score, empty reason). G-Eval is a commonly-used LLM-based grading mechanism; users evaluating complex outputs where values may be empty get no indication of what went wrong. This violates the principle of giving users useful eval feedback.

source_issues.title: handleGEval returns NaN score and silent false-fail when value is an empty array
source_issues.evidence: Empty array in g-eval assertion value causes 0/0 division resulting in NaN score and silent false-fail with empty reason string. User gets no actionable feedback. Identified root cause in src/assertions/geval.ts lines 38-45.

signals.topic: not-javascript assertion type produces incorrect results for non-boolean value types
signals.summary: The `not-javascript` assertion type does not properly handle the inverse condition for value types other than boolean. Assertions that should fail incorrectly pass when `value` is a number, function, or object. The inverse logic is only applied for boolean values, leaving other types broken.
signals.review_reason: Assertion logic produces incorrect pass/fail results — assertions that should fail silently pass. This undermines the reliability of eval results; users cannot trust their test outcomes when using not-javascript assertions with non-boolean values.

source_issues.title: assertion type: "not-javascript" doesn't work in all cases
source_issues.evidence: not-javascript assertion with value as a function/object/number should fail but incorrectly passes. Inverse handling in handleJavascript() only applies to boolean value types, leaving number/function/object value types broken.

signals.topic: vLLM LLM wrapper breaks completely with vLLM>=0.19.0 due to removed 'best_of' parameter — TypeError on every .complete() call
signals.summary: llama-index-llms-vllm 0.7.0 unconditionally passes 'best_of' to vLLM's SamplingParams, but vLLM>=0.19.0 removed that parameter. Every .complete() call immediately raises TypeError, making the entire vLLM integration unusable with current vLLM versions.
signals.review_reason: vLLM integration is completely unusable with current vLLM versions. Every single .complete() call throws TypeError at base.py:292, blocking the entire LLM invocation path. This is a main-flow failure with clear traceback, reproducible steps, and no workaround in the official wrapper.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index-llms-vllm: best_of removed from vLLM SamplingParams causes TypeError on .complete()
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'best_of' raised at every .complete() call. Reproduction: pip install llama-index==0.14.20 llama-index-llms-vllm==0.7.0 vllm==0.19.0; then llm.complete('Hello') throws immediately.

signals.topic: PDFReader with S3 file path fails due to Path() converting S3 URIs to invalid WindowsPath — blocks PDF loading from S3
signals.summary: PDFReader.load_data() unconditionally casts input to Path(), converting S3-style URIs (e.g., 'bucket/key/file.pdf') into WindowsPath objects ('bucket\key\file.pdf'). s3fs then raises ValueError: Attempt to open non key-like path, making PDF loading from S3 completely broken.
signals.review_reason: Core file loading functionality (PDF from S3) is completely blocked. The PDFReader unconditionally uses Path() which corrupts S3 URIs. This is a main-flow failure in a commonly used data ingestion pattern (S3 → PDF parsing → RAG pipeline). Marked P1 by maintainers, consistent with severity.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: impossible to use PDFReader with an S3 file because of Path() casting
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: Attempt to open non key-like path raised when using SimpleDirectoryReader with s3fs. Path() converts 'bucket/key/file.pdf' to WindowsPath 'bucket\key\file.pdf', causing s3fs.S3File to reject it. Full stack trace provided.

signals.topic: Bedrock converse async streaming: @retry_decorator on async generator is silently inert — retries never fire for streaming calls
signals.summary: llms/bedrock_converse/utils.py decorates _conversion_stream_with_retry with tenacity's @retry_decorator, but the function contains 'yield', making it an async generator. Tenacity only wraps the initial call (which merely creates the generator object), so exceptions during iteration are never retried. ThrottlingException and ServiceUnavailableException during streaming calls are silently swallowed.
signals.review_reason: Retries are silently disabled for Bedrock streaming LLM calls. When ThrottlingException or ServiceUnavailableException occurs mid-stream, the call fails without retry — a silent failure that degrades reliability of a key LLM integration. The bug is architecturally confirmed (async generator + tenacity incompatibility) and acknowledged by code comments.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @retry_decorator on async generator _conversion_stream_with_retry is silently inert
source_issues.evidence: Bug is confirmed via a minimal reproducible example showing tenacity on async generators never fires. The code comment at line 861 even acknowledges the issue as 'a bit of a hack'. Stream failures due to ThrottlingException/ServiceUnavailableException during Bedrock streaming calls are silently not retried.

signals.topic: FunctionAgent returns empty response on second .run() call — context/state not persisted across calls
signals.summary: When using FunctionAgent with a Context object across multiple .run() calls, the second call returns an empty response. The first call correctly uses the stored context (e.g., remembers 'my name is Laurie'), but the second call produces no output despite the context documentation indicating state should be preserved.
signals.review_reason: Core agent session state is broken: the second .run() call produces empty output, completely undermining multi-turn conversation workflows. This is not an edge case — it blocks the fundamental use case of agents maintaining context across turns. The issue is explicitly contradicted by official documentation.

source_issues.title: [Question]: why the second response is empty?
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: run(FunctionAgent, 'Hi my name is Laurie') → correct response. Run same ctx, 'what's my name?' → empty response. Official documentation at developers.llamaindex.ai shows this should work, indicating a regression or design gap.

signals.topic: to_openai_message_dict does not JSON-serialize tool_kwargs — breaks cross-provider agent workflows (Anthropic → OpenAI)
signals.summary: When using AgentWorkflow with mixed LLM providers (e.g., Anthropic orchestrator handing off to OpenAI/AzureOpenAI sub-agent), the OpenAI Chat Completions API returns 400 BadRequestError because tool_kwargs dict is placed into function.arguments without json.dumps(). Anthropic stores tool_kwargs as a dict; OpenAI requires a JSON string.
signals.review_reason: Cross-provider agent workflows (Anthropic → OpenAI/AzureOpenAI handoffs) fail with 400 BadRequestError. This blocks a key multi-agent orchestration pattern. The root cause is a one-line fix (json.dumps on tool_kwargs) that was already correctly implemented in the Responses API path but omitted from the Chat Completions path.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs and breaks cross-provider agent workflows
source_issues.evidence: BadRequestError: 400 - expected a string for 'messages[3].tool_calls[0].function.arguments', but got an object. Triggered when Anthropic agent hands off to OpenAI agent in AgentWorkflow. The same pattern is already correctly handled in to_openai_responses_message_dict but missed in to_openai_message_dict.

signals.topic: MCP tools fail on Windows due to process.cwd() resolving to System32 causing EPERM errors
signals.summary: All MCP tool file-write operations use process.cwd() which on Windows resolves to C:\Windows\System32 (read-only), causing every stateful MCP tool to fail with EPERM. Affects 16+ files in mcp-tools/.
signals.review_reason: Critical user-impact bug: ALL MCP tool state writes fail on Windows with EPERM, blocking every stateful MCP tool operation. 16+ files affected. This is a complete blocker for Windows users.

source_issues.title: MCP tools use process.cwd() which resolves to System32 on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Every MCP tool file uses process.cwd() to build paths like .claude-flow/swarm/. On Windows, npx launches with process.cwd()=C:\Windows\System32, causing EPERM on all writes. 16+ files affected. No workaround.

signals.topic: CLI lazy-loaded commands silently mis-route to wrong handler when core command keywords appear in argv
signals.summary: Commands like 'ruflo daemon start' silently route to the top-level 'start' command instead of the daemon subcommand. Affects all lazy-loaded commands (daemon, doctor, embeddings, neural, config, workflow, hive-mind) when any of 10 core sync keywords appear later in argv.
signals.review_reason: User-experience catastrophe: commands silently execute the wrong handler with no error or warning. A user running 'ruflo daemon start --foreground' gets the wrong command with no indication anything is wrong. Entire lazy-loaded command subsystem is unreliable.

source_issues.title: CLI: lazy-loaded commands silently mis-route when a core sync command name follows in argv
source_issues.evidence: ruflo daemon start routes to top-level 'start' instead of daemon subcommand. Every lazy-loaded command (daemon, doctor, embeddings, neural, config, workflow, hive-mind) affected. No error shown to user. Commands silently do wrong thing.

signals.topic: ruflo init --skip-claude overwrites user config at ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md without backup despite documentation promising to skip .claude/ directory
signals.summary: The --skip-claude flag's documentation states 'Skip .claude/ directory creation (runtime only)' but the code overwrites the global Claude Code config file ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with a stub and creates no backup.
signals.review_reason: Data loss bug: user config silently destroyed with no backup and behavior contradicts documented flag contract. Users relying on --skip-claude expecting it to be safe lose their Claude Code configuration.

source_issues.title: init --skip-claude overwrites ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md without backup
source_issues.evidence: Running 'ruflo init --skip-claude --minimal' overwrote the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (Claude Code's global configuration) with a 4-line stub. No backup was created. The --skip-claude documentation promises to skip .claude/ directory creation.

signals.topic: All ruflo memory subcommands (init, stats, store, search, list, cleanup, compress) hang indefinitely after completion due to ONNX/WASM worker threads preventing process exit
signals.summary: Every 'ruflo memory' subcommand hangs after completing its work because ONNX embedding model worker threads (from @xenova/transformers) keep the Node.js event loop alive. Process never exits.
signals.review_reason: Workflow-blocking: every memory subcommand hangs indefinitely, preventing automation scripts, CI pipelines, and normal CLI usage from completing. User must manually kill the process.

source_issues.title: fix: ruflo memory subcommands hang after completion - process.exit() missing from CLI entry point
source_issues.evidence: All 'ruflo memory' subcommands (init, stats, store, search, list, cleanup, compress) hang indefinitely after completing work. ONNX/WASM worker threads keep Node.js event loop alive. Root cause: ensureInitialized() loads ONNX embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) which spawns threads never terminated.

signals.topic: npm install fails on Windows (v3.5.78) due to Invalid Version error from koa-router@14.0.0 dependency tree, blocking initial setup
signals.summary: Running 'npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init --wizard' on Windows fails immediately with 'npm error Invalid Version:' due to a semver parsing error in koa-router@14.0.0's dependency tree.
signals.review_reason: Onboarding blocker on Windows: new users cannot install or initialize the CLI due to a dependency version conflict. This is a primary acquisition funnel failure.

source_issues.title: npm error: Invalid Version in koa-router@14.0.0 dependency tree (v3.5.78)
source_issues.evidence: npm error Invalid Version: on Windows 11 with npm 11.11.0 and Node 24.14.1. 'npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init --wizard' fails immediately. Stack trace shows TypeError: Invalid Version in semver compare, traced to koa-router@14.0.0.

signals.topic: Chrome `--no-sandbox` not configurable — browser unusable in containers, VMs, and Linux server environments
signals.summary: Chrome crashes immediately on startup in containerized/VM/server environments (Docker, cloud VMs, CI runners, Ubuntu 23.10+, NAS systems) due to Chromium sandbox restrictions when running as root. The tool provides no way to pass `--no-sandbox` or other container-required Chrome flags, making browser automation completely unavailable in these environments.
aliases: chrome crashes as root in containers
browser unusable in cloud CI environments
agent dashboard no chrome launch args
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues spanning 14 months confirm this is a recurring, unresolved blocker. The browser is completely unusable in containerized and server environments (Docker, cloud VMs, CI runners, NAS) — which are the primary deployment targets for AI agents using agent-browser. The error is silent in some cases (hangs) and crashes in others, with no user-facing guidance. AI coding agents running in cloud environments (the documented primary use case per issue #70) are entirely blocked.

source_issues.title: Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported. See https://crbug.com/638180.
source_issues.evidence: Chrome crashes with 'Page crashed' when running as root in containerized environments. Explicit use case: AI coding agents (Claude Code) in cloud environments need browser automation but cannot use it without --no-sandbox. Agent-browser v0.5.0 affected. Includes required Chromium flags list.

source_issues.title: Add Chrome launch args support in Agent Dashboard UI (needed for `--no-sandbox` on some Linux/VM/container setups)
source_issues.evidence: Chrome exits immediately before exposing DevTools URL with FATAL: content/browser/zygote_host/zygote_host_impl_linux.cc:128 No usable sandbox! error. Agent Dashboard UI provides no option to pass custom Chrome launch arguments. Lists Docker containers, cloud VMs, CI runners, hardened Linux hosts as affected environments. Error shown in attached screenshot.

source_issues.title: agent-browser open hangs on Linux Server/NAS - daemon fails to start (OpenClaw agent)
source_issues.evidence: Daemon hangs indefinitely on Linux Server/NAS (Ubuntu 24.04) with all system dependencies installed. No socket file created, no Chrome process spawned. Reporter is OpenClaw AI agent — browser automation completely blocked. Author explicitly hypothesizes root cause is missing --no-sandbox for server environment. Agent running on Linux Server/NAS cannot use the tool at all.

signals.topic: `--auto-connect` triggers duplicate DevTools remote-debugging permission prompts due to legacy discovery ordering
signals.summary: When using `--auto-connect` to attach to an existing Chrome instance, the tool first calls legacy discovery endpoints (`/json/version`, `/json/list`) before falling back to the exact DevToolsActivePort websocket path. This causes two separate remote-debugging permission prompts from Chrome instead of one, degrading the UX for UI remote-debugging mode.
aliases: multiple remote debugging prompts auto connect
signals.review_reason: Duplicate permission prompts are a UX degradation that interrupts automated workflows — every `--auto-connect` session requires the user to manually approve two browser prompts. While not a complete workflow blocker, this is a friction point that users explicitly notice and ask about (issue #1206). The fix is well-understood (reorder discovery) but impacts the auto-connect workflow daily.

source_issues.title: Prefer DevToolsActivePort websocket path first in --auto-connect to avoid duplicate remote-debugging prompts
source_issues.evidence: Issue describes the exact discovery order causing two prompts: legacy discovery probing (one prompt) then real websocket attach (second prompt). Proposes using the DevToolsActivePort websocket path first and falling back to legacy only if that fails.

source_issues.title: Is it normal to always have to allow twice when connecting to an existing Chrome instance via --auto-connect?
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly asking if the double-prompt behavior is expected on agent-browser 0.25.3. Confirms the duplicate-permission issue is a real user-observed behavior on the current version.

signals.topic: Multi-agent cookie isolation gap: CDP BrowserContext not used, cookies leak between concurrent sessions on same Chrome instance
signals.summary: When multiple AI agents connect to the same Chrome instance via `--auto-connect` or `connect <port>`, all sessions share the default BrowserContext — meaning cookies, localStorage, and sessionStorage leak between sessions. This makes it impossible to run two agents against the same domain with different credentials (e.g. two Google accounts, staging vs production).
signals.review_reason: Multi-agent workflows on the same Chrome instance are a documented use case, and cookie leakage between sessions breaks the fundamental assumption of session isolation. When two agents target the same domain with different credentials, the second login overwrites the first — silently corrupting both agents' state. This has been a known issue since January 2026 (#86) and affects both `--auto-connect` and `connect` modes with no workaround currently available.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request] CDP BrowserContext support for cookie-isolated parallel sessions
source_issues.evidence: Describes the root cause: `--session` provides tab-namespace isolation but does NOT create a CDP `Target.createBrowserContext` — so no storage isolation. Documents three agents (university admin, personal cloud, infrastructure) on the same Chrome instance where cookies would collide if targeting the same domain. Explicitly lists three prior related issues (#86, #326, #896) and notes that `--auto-connect` has no equivalent fix to the daemon-mode profile scoping.

source_issues.title: Support for Multi Session
source_issues.evidence: Original multi-session bug report: two agents using agent-browser simultaneously in different Tmux panes had browser content intercept each other. User explicitly observed 'They seems shared the same playwright browser instance.' Confirmed cross-session interference in multi-agent production use.

signals.topic: `get box` and `get styles` commands return only "Done" in text mode with no actual data
signals.summary: In non-JSON text output mode, `agent-browser get box` and `agent-browser get styles` print only `✓ Done` instead of the element's bounding box or computed styles. All other `get` subcommands (`get text`, `get html`, `get value`, `get count`, `get attr`) print their data correctly — this is regression-specific to `box` and `styles`. JSON mode is unaffected.
aliases: get box text mode no output
get styles text mode silent failure
box and styles commands output only Done
signals.review_reason: Commands silently return no actionable data in text mode. Users running the CLI in its default output mode get `✓ Done` for box and styles queries with zero indication of failure. While JSON mode works, the default text output path is broken, making the tool confusing and unreliable for the majority of users who don't use `--json`. This is a visible functional gap — not a cosmetic issue.

source_issues.title: `get box` and `get styles` print only "Done" in text mode
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full repro steps: `get box @e1` and `get styles @e1` print `✓ Done` with no data in text mode. Workaround uses `--json` mode. Other `get` subcommands in the same family work correctly, isolating this to the box and styles text-mode output path.

signals.topic: iOS provider cannot reach mounted DOM elements on local Next.js dev routes — agent-native parity gap
signals.summary: When using the iOS provider (`-p ios`), the browser opens local Next.js dev routes (e.g. `localhost:3100`) but only exposes the Next shell/scaffold HTML, never the mounted page's actual DOM. Selectors like `#placeholder-ime` are always element-not-found. The same route works fine with direct Appium + XCUITest Safari, confirming the page itself is functional.
aliases: iOS provider mounted DOM not accessible
iOS provider local dev server selector not found
iOS Safari mounted page DOM not reachable
signals.review_reason: The iOS provider is a first-class, documented mode of agent-browser. When it silently fails to reach the actual mounted page content, all downstream commands (click, type, eval) fail silently. This creates a complete parity gap between what a human tester can do in iOS Safari and what an agent can do — making the iOS provider effectively unusable for any local dev workflow. The workaround is not viable (replacing the entire tool with Appium).

source_issues.title: iOS provider opens local Next dev route but never exposes mounted page selectors
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with exact repro steps: open local Slate examples site on macOS, run a batch of commands via iOS provider. The URL resolves correctly but `#placeholder-ime` is always null. Direct Appium + XCUITest on the same machine CAN read the real editor HTML, ruling out a page bug. Explicitly labeled as an 'agent-native parity gap' — human can see the page but the agent cannot.

signals.topic: MCP protocol version header not downgraded after negotiation — blocks MCP client creation against older servers
signals.summary: HttpMCPTransport and SseMCPTransport always send the latest MCP protocol version in headers after initialization instead of the negotiated version, causing 400 errors against servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP that only support older versions. createMCPClient() never resolves.
signals.review_reason: MCP client creation is completely blocked — main flow fails with a non-resolving promise. Clear, reproducible evidence with a real server. Single issue qualifies for P0 given severity (complete functional block of a primary API).

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/mcp] Streamable HTTP transport does not downgrade `mcp-protocol-version` header after version negotiation (breaks servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP)
source_issues.evidence: Post-initialization HTTP requests return 400 with 'Unsupported protocol version'; createMCPClient() never resolves. Repro against real Figma Desktop MCP server provided.

signals.topic: Gateway fallback to Gemini thinking models drops thinkingConfig — AI_NoObjectGeneratedError breaks structured output
signals.summary: When Vercel AI Gateway falls back to Gemini 2.5 thinking models via providerOptions.gateway.models, providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: false is not forwarded. Gemini returns thinking tokens, breaking Output.object() parsing with non-retryable AI_NoObjectGeneratedError.
signals.review_reason: Main structured output flow fails non-retryably. The error is a complete block for any user relying on gateway fallback + Output.object() + Gemini thinking models. Provides explicit stack trace and full repro.

source_issues.title: providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: false ignored for gateway-fallback models — thinking tokens break Output.object() parsing
source_issues.evidence: AI_NoObjectGeneratedError thrown on every request falling back to Gemini 2.5 via gateway.models. Stack trace provided. Non-retryable parsing error. false sense of safety from includeThoughts: false.

signals.topic: Gateway fallback routes to providers outside the configured order — compliance/cost boundary violation
signals.summary: providerOptions.gateway.order constraints are not applied to models selected via providerOptions.gateway.models fallback list. Traffic silently routes through unexpected providers (e.g. xai routed via deepinfra) not listed in order, with no warning or error.
aliases: gateway fallback routes through unlisted provider
signals.review_reason: Silent provider boundary violation — user-configured constraints are silently ignored. Traffic can unexpectedly route to unlisted providers causing compliance, cost, and latency implications with zero visibility. Explicit root cause traced to independent routing mechanisms.

source_issues.title: providerOptions.gateway.order not respected when routing via providerOptions.gateway.models — unexpected provider (deepinfra) selected
source_issues.evidence: order: ['openai', 'google', 'azure'] silently bypassed for xai/grok-4.1-fast-non-reasoning in gateway.models. Traffic routes through deepinfra. No error or warning. Compliance and cost implications with no observability.

signals.topic: streamFunctionCallArguments never emits tool-call for array-typed arguments — tool execute() never runs
signals.summary: Vertex AI (Gemini 3 Flash) terminal streaming chunk for array args has partialArgs but omits willContinue, failing the isTerminalChunk check. tool-input-end and tool-call events are never emitted; the tool's execute() function is never called.
aliases: Vertex tool call not emitted for array args
signals.review_reason: Tool execution is completely suppressed for any tool with array-typed arguments on Vertex/Gemini. Main agentic workflow is blocked — tool results never delivered and tool never executes. Clear stream trace evidence provided.

source_issues.title: streamFunctionCallArguments: tool-call never emitted for array args (terminal chunk has partialArgs)
source_issues.evidence: tool-input-start and tool-input-delta fire but tool-input-end and tool-call never emit. execute() is never called. Full stream output shown: start, start-step, tool-input-start, tool-input-delta, finish-step, finish — with tool-call, tool-result missing.

signals.topic: Race condition in runToolsTransformation: flush closes stream before tool result is registered — tool results silently lost
signals.summary: outstandingToolResults counter is incremented after await parseToolCall(), but flush() can fire during that await and see size===0, closing the stream prematurely. Tool executes successfully but its result is lost, producing 'Tool execution aborted'. Observed consistently in Bun v1.3.11.
signals.review_reason: Tool results are silently lost in agentic workflows. Tool executes but consumer never receives the result. Affects runtime environments (Bun) where TransformStream flush timing is different. Complete trace evidence showing the exact race sequence.

source_issues.title: Race condition in runToolsTransformation: flush closes stream before async transform registers tool
source_issues.evidence: Trace shows: tool-call pending → flush fires with outstanding=0 → stream closes → tool START → tool RESOLVED → 'Tool execution aborted'. Tool executes but result has no destination. Consistent repro in Bun v1.3.11.

signals.topic: Malformed Origin header in Server Actions CSRF validation causes unhandled TypeError, returning HTTP 500 instead of 400, enabling DoS attacks on self-hosted Next.js deployments
signals.summary: The new URL(originHeader) call in Server Actions CSRF check throws an unhandled TypeError on malformed Origin headers (e.g. 'http://', 'Origin: null'). The exception propagates uncaught, causing HTTP 500 responses. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger continuous 500 errors on any page with Server Actions without knowing action IDs. This affects all v14.x through v16.2.3 stable; v15.5.x stable lacks even the 'null' guard that canary added. Vercel CDN masks the issue (edge normalizes Origin).
aliases: Server Actions malformed Origin header DoS

signals.topic: Turbopack chunk filenames containing ~ (tilde) character are blocked by enterprise WAFs, causing entire app to fail loading in production self-hosted deployments behind standard WAF rulesets

The browser refuses to execute the file due to MIME type mismatch, breaking the app entirely. Not present in 16.1.x which used hex-only hashes. Only affects self-hosted enterprise deployments; not reproducible on Vercel.

signals.topic: SIGKILL to turbo run leaves child processes orphaned; SIGINT not forwarded to tasks — blocks Playwright CI and graceful shutdown
signals.summary: When the turbo run process receives SIGKILL (e.g., from Playwright test runner or CI job cancellation), child processes (dev servers, build tasks) continue running as orphans. Additionally, SIGINT is not forwarded to underlying tasks, preventing graceful shutdown. This directly breaks Playwright + turbo integration (Playwright sends SIGKILL on test close) and any CI pipeline that relies on process cleanup.
signals.review_reason: SIGKILL causing orphaned child processes directly breaks a mainstream CI testing pattern (Playwright webServer). SIGINT not forwarded prevents graceful shutdown of tasks. Both issues make turbo incompatible with standard CI cancellation and testing lifecycle signals. 2 independent issues with clear reproduction steps confirm this is a systemic signal handling defect, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: On SIGKILL to `turbo run`, tasks continue running (incompatible with Playwright testing)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps: run `turbo run dev`, kill the turbo process with `kill -9`, dev server remains running on port 3000. Playwright sends SIGKILL on test close, making turbo incompatible with Playwright webServer config. User confirms this works correctly when using `next dev` directly instead of `turbo run dev`.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` being sent to `turbo` is not forwarded to underlying tasks
source_issues.evidence: User reports `kill -SIGINT ${TURBO_PID}` does not result in SIGINT being sent to child tasks. No graceful shutdown of running tasks occurs on Ctrl+C. 22 comments indicating ongoing discussion and recent activity.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker with pnpm: missing stub files for bin entries breaks multi-stage Docker build workflow
signals.summary: Users running `turbo prune --docker` with pnpm encounter build failures because prune only outputs package.json files, not stub files for bin entries. This prevents pnpm from generating shims in .bin, breaking the `copy prune json -> pnpm install -> copy full -> turbo build` multi-stage sequence when any dependent package exposes a CLI tool.
signals.review_reason: Docker multi-stage builds with pnpm are a mainstream CI pattern. `turbo prune --docker` produces incomplete output that causes pnpm to skip .bin shim creation, which directly breaks dependent build steps. The user provides a complete reproduction showing the failure in a real Docker workflow.

source_issues.title: prune --docker: create stub source files for bin entries

signals.topic: Git source control filter (`--filter="[origin/main..HEAD]"`) fails to detect changes, causing incorrect/incomplete task execution
signals.summary: When using turbo with a source control filter like `--filter="[origin/main..HEAD]"`, turbo does not detect the same changes that `git show origin/main..HEAD` reports. This leads to turbo skipping tasks for packages that were actually modified, resulting in stale builds. Using `--affected` works around the issue.
signals.review_reason: The git source control filter is a core feature for partial builds in CI. When it silently skips tasks for packages that were actually modified, it produces stale/incomplete build artifacts. This is a correctness issue that undermines trust in turbo's caching logic, with a clear reproducible test case.

source_issues.title: Filtering by source control changes doesn't detect changes
source_issues.evidence: User shows `git show origin/main..HEAD` outputs the commit but `turbo run lint --dry=json --filter="[origin/main..HEAD]"` returns zero directories; `--affected` correctly returns the modified package. Reproducible via provided reproduction repo.
